# Claude Code mods

Function-hook plugins ("Claude Mods"), built 2026-10-02 from the session audit
(`/watch` of Chase AI's "Claude Mods" video + a read of the last 30 transcripts).
Synced to both machines through the `~/.claude` repo.

| Mod | Event | Shows | Usage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo-band` | `turn.complete`, timer | Band: `repos: 3 dirty · 1 unpushed`, **Closeout** / **Closeout + exit** buttons; `/repos` lists them | none (local git) |
| `next-steps` | `session.start`, `turn.complete` | Band: 3 buttons. At start, newest `docs/handoffs/*.md`; after a turn, Haiku's suggestions. A press fills the prompt box to edit; Enter sends. `/next-steps off\|on` | one Haiku call per answered turn |
| `job-watch` | `session.start`, 10-min timer, task notifications | Status line: scheduled jobs, `errors.log`, recall eval; toasts when a job runs or a background task finishes; `/jobs` | none |
| `merge-cleanup` | after a `gh pr merge` Bash/PowerShell call | Toast naming the branches/worktrees removed (verified merged only; see `feedback_post-merge-cleanup`) | none |
| `where` | after Write/Edit/NotebookEdit | `/where [filter]` pane of recent files with copy-path buttons | none |
| `twin-copy-guard` | around Write/Edit/NotebookEdit, `turn.complete` | At turn end, names a hook/skill twin left unpatched (`~/.claude/hooks` ↔ `~/.codex/hooks`, `~/.claude/skills` ↔ `~/.agents/skills`) and offers **Copy across** when the pair matched before the edit; `/twins` lists every differing pair | none |
| `config-encoding-guard` | `session.start`, after Write/Edit/Bash/PowerShell, `turn.complete` | Catches a UTF-8 BOM or CP1252 garbling (`â€”`, `â–“`) in `~/.claude`/`~/.codex` config (see `project_settings-json-bom-trap`); offers a repair that keeps `.encoding-bak` and never writes JSON that will not parse; `/encoding` | none |
| `slate-status` | `session.start`, 30-min timer | Status line: `slate: DUE · 1/5 active · 2 to do` from `project-triage/portfolio.py slate-check`; toasts when it changes and is not OK; `/slate` lists problems | none |
| `landed` | `session.start` (background scan) | `/landed [today\|week\|N] [refresh] [project]`: files created or changed, grouped by project, both machines, from `project-triage/landed.py` | none |

Added 2026-10-03 (from the Nate Herk mods video + a 45-day transcript audit):
`repo-band` now fetches every repo once at session start, shows `↓N` behind, and
before Claude's first edit in a repo each session fetches it and asks **Pull first /
Edit anyway / Cancel** when it is behind origin. `job-watch` now shows `milvus ✓/✗`
(Docker-hosted Milvus for memsearch) and toasts when it goes down; machines with no
milvus container show nothing.

Windows note: on this machine `~/.codex/hooks` is not a mirror (1 file), and 6 of the
skills in `~/.claude/skills` are junctions into `~/.agents/skills` (same file, never
flagged). The other ~42 are real copies, so twin drift there is real (`harvest`
differed on 2026-10-03).

## Loading

**The folder is the list.** Every folder here with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` loads on both
machines, unless it has a `.disabled` file or fails `claude plugin validate`. Nothing is
hand-listed (set 2026-10-03; before that the list lived in three places and drifted).

- `mods-sync.ps1` (Windows) sets the user env var `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`.
- `mods-sync.sh` (Mac) writes `~/.claude/mods/.loadlist` (gitignored); `~/.zshrc` reads it:
  ```sh
  [ -f ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist ] && export CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS="$(cat ~/.claude/mods/.loadlist)"
  ```
- `dev-sync` and `closeout` run the sync and report one line:
  `mods: 8 loaded, 1 disabled, 0 invalid`. A broken mod is named and left out, never loaded.
- Turn one off on both machines: `touch ~/.claude/mods/<name>/.disabled`, commit, sync.
  Turn it back on: delete the file.
- A changed list takes effect after a restart of Claude Code (and a new shell on the Mac).

Headless `claude -p` runs report "hooks modules are turned off ... rollout switch
served off" (seen 2026-10-02); the mods are for interactive sessions.

## Checking

```sh
claude plugin validate ~/.claude/mods/<mod>
claude plugin test ~/.claude/mods/<mod>     # needs the rollout switch on
```

1	---
2	name: dev-sync
3	description: >-
4	  Bring this machine into line with GitHub and load back the context that came with it:
5	  locate DEV automatically, pull config and skills, inventory every project, commit and
6	  push local work, pull the other machine's work, clone what is missing, report
7	  conflicts, then read the repo's STATUS and latest handoff and report where the last
8	  session left off. Use when Eric switches machines, sits down to start work, says 'sync
9	  DEV', asks whether everything is pushed, or asks where he left off. Do not use when
10	  Eric says '/startup' or 'good morning' (use startup, which runs this sync) or to
11	  scaffold a new repo (use new-project).
12	---
13	
14	# DEV sync
15	
16	Eric works on a Mac and a Windows laptop. GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport. This skill makes the current machine match GitHub without losing anything on either side. It is the first thing to run when sitting down at a machine.
17	
18	## Step 0: find DEV (never depend on cwd)
19	
20	Eric may run this from anywhere. Detect the machine and go to its DEV root:
21	
22	- macOS (`uname` = Darwin): `~/DEV`
23	- Windows (PowerShell, or `$OS` = Windows_NT): `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV`
24	
25	If that folder does not exist, stop and say so. Do not guess another location. Print the root you chose on the first line of output.
26	
27	## Step 1: config and skills
28	
29	These are separate repos and the other machine may have changed them:
30	
31	1. `~/.claude` (repo `dotclaude`): `git pull`. If `~/.claude/machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` or `machine.windows.md` to `machine.md` for this OS. Then sync the mods: `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` (Windows). The folder is the list; put its one line (`mods: N loaded, N disabled, N invalid`) in the report and name any invalid mod. Then apply the 7-day rule: `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply` (`portfolio_json` in `_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It pauses any project started more than 7 days ago with no receiver and no step 1 done, and prints one line plus each project paused or on the clock; put that in the report.
32	2. `~/.claude/skills` (repo `claude-skills`): `git pull`, then run `sync-to-codex.sh` (Mac) or `sync-to-codex.ps1` (Windows) so Codex sees the shared skills.
33	3. `~/.claude/global-memory` (repo `claude-global-memory`): `git pull`. **This is the only thing that carries memory between the two machines.** USER.md, MEMORY.md and the handoffs live here. `daily-backup` pushes this repo nightly, but nothing pulled it at the start of a session until this step existed, so a same-day handoff (worked on the Mac after lunch, picked up on Windows that evening) arrived with stale memory. Pull it before anything else reads it. If the pull brings in commits, say how many and name the newest, so it is visible that memory moved.
34	
35	If any of the three has local uncommitted changes, commit them first with `<machine> snapshot before sync`, then pull, then push.
36	
37	4. **Mirror project memory across the two slugs.** Tier A memory is keyed by a slug built from the absolute path, so every project has a Mac folder (`-Users-kristinarash-DEV-X`) and a Windows folder (`C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV-X`) under `~/.claude/projects/`. dotclaude carries both to both machines, but each machine auto-loads only its own. Before this step existed, 43 memories written on the Mac never loaded on Windows (found 2026-09-24). After the pulls above, run:
38	
39	   - Mac: `python3 ~/.claude/skills/dev-sync/mirror_memory.py`
40	   - Windows: `python $HOME\.claude\skills\dev-sync\mirror_memory.py`
41	
42	   It copies files one side lacks, lets the newer version win when both have one (frontmatter `modified:`, else last commit), merges `MEMORY.md` indexes line by line, creates the twin folder when a project has memory on only one machine, and never deletes. The older side of any replaced file stays in dotclaude history. Put its summary line in the Step 4 report. If it wrote anything, commit `~/.claude` with `<machine> memory mirror` and push, so the other machine gets the result on its next sync.
43	
44	   Mirroring is a union: a memory deleted on one machine comes back from the other. To retire a memory for good, delete it from both slug folders in the same commit.
45	
46	Merge note for `global-memory`: `transcripts/.errors.log` and `MEMORY.md` are both append-heavy and both machines write them. On conflict, keep both sides' content rather than choosing one — these are logs, not settings, and a dropped line is a lost memory.
47	
48	## Step 2: inventory (always show before changing anything)
49	
50	Walk `DEV/*`, `DEV/Football/*`, and `DEV/SpecialRequests/*`. Skip `.claude`, `_tools`, `_DRIVE` (a link to the Google Drive primary storage drive, not a project; never init it, never walk into it), `token-dashboard` (someone else's remote), and any folder ending in `_OLD_merged*`. For each folder report one of:
51	
52	- **repo + erash11 remote**: uncommitted count, unpushed count
53	- **repo, no remote**: needs `gh repo create`
54	- **not a repo**: needs init + create (use the `new-project` skill's file set)
55	
56	Then `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --json name` and list repos with no local folder. Skip: `dotclaude` (that is `~/.claude`), `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`, `claude-memory-compiler`, `DEV`, `DexaProject`.
57	
58	Eric pre-approves these operations; the inventory is for visibility, not a pause for approval, unless something looks wrong (a repo with hundreds of uncommitted files, a large file about to be added).
59	
60	**Group the report by activity, not alphabetically.** Run `~/.claude/scripts/dev-activity.sh` (Mac) or `dev-activity.ps1` (Windows), which ranks repos by distinct commit days over 90 days. List the active ones individually and collapse the rest to a count: "118 dormant repos: all clean" is the useful line, not 118 names. About 14 repos are genuinely worked at any time; the rest are archives that happen to live in the same folder.
61	
62	Rank by **commit days, not recency**. On 2026-09-09 a bulk migration gave 43 repos one commit each, after which every one of them looked active by any recency measure. Days-worked is not fooled by that, because a migration touches a repo once.
63	
64	Nothing is archived or moved on the strength of this. Sorting is a reporting concern. Moving a dormant repo into an archive folder would break three things at once: `harvest-dev-docs` reads `<dir>/docs/*.md` without recursing, so archived repos would silently drop out of the memsearch index; KeystoneOS `projects.json`, `memory-sources.json`, `memory-index-paths.json` and `discovery-roots.json` hold DEV paths; and Tier A project memory is keyed by a slug derived from the absolute path, so moving a repo orphans its memory. Checked 2026-09-12. Do not revive the archive idea without fixing all three first.
65	
66	## Step 3: apply, per repo
67	
68	1. If uncommitted: put any untracked file over 95 MB and any `.env` into `.gitignore`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
69	2. `git fetch origin` then `git merge --no-edit origin/<branch>`.
70	3. On conflict: keep this machine's version, save the remote version beside it as `<file>.from-mac` or `<file>.from-windows` (whichever the other machine is), stage both, commit. Never discard either side. `.DS_Store` conflicts: just delete the file.
71	
72	   Save the remote side by **moving the file, never by redirecting stdout**. A
73	   redirect re-encodes the bytes; on Windows that silently mangles every
74	   non-ASCII character (an em-dash becomes `ΓÇö`) and adds a UTF-8 BOM, so the
75	   saved copy is corrupt and every later diff shows a phantom first-line change.
76	
77	   - PowerShell: `git checkout --theirs -- <f>; Move-Item <f> <f>.from-mac; git checkout --ours -- <f>`
78	   - bash: `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-mac && git checkout --ours -- <f>`
79	
80	   Never run `git add -A` while `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists — it stages the
81	   conflict markers themselves and commits a broken file. Stage only the named
82	   paths you just resolved.
83	4. `git push`.
84	5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> DEV/<name>`.
85	6. No remote: `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.
86	
87	Windows note: line-ending noise (`LF will be replaced by CRLF`) is normal. If a merge refuses to start because of phantom modifications, run `git add --renormalize .` and commit before merging.
88	
89	Stale-lock note: if a commit or push fails with `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`, check
90	`pgrep -fl git` (or `Get-Process git`) first. If no git is running and the
91	`.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale from an
92	interrupted run. Move it aside — do not delete it — then retry.
93	
94	## Step 4: verify and report
95	
96	Re-walk every repo. Report: DEV root used, config and skills pulled (yes/no), the memory-mirror summary line, repos checked, pulled, cloned, created, and any folder still dirty or unpushed. List every `.from-*` file created so Eric can reconcile them. Finish with one line: clean or not.
97	
98	## Step 5: pick up where the other machine left off
99	
100	Syncing git state is only half the job. The other half is loading the context that came with it, and nothing else does this — the SessionStart hook injects global memory, but project state lives in the repo, and Tier A project memory only crosses machines through the Step 1 mirror. This step is the only place that repo context gets read back in.
101	
102	Do this for the repo Eric names, or the one he is in. If he has not named one, pick from the ACTIVE list in Step 2, not from all 132: take the active repo with the most recent commit and say which you chose. A dormant repo receiving one migration commit must never win this, which is exactly what picking by recency across everything would do.
103	
104	1. Read `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md` if there is no AGENTS.md).
105	2. Read `<repo>/docs/STATUS.md`.
106	3. Read the newest file in `<repo>/docs/handoffs/`, if the folder exists and its newest file is within about two weeks.
107	4. If `docs/STATUS.md` does not exist in a repo that has real work in it, say so — that repo is invisible to the other machine and closeout should have created it.
108	
109	Then report, in six lines or fewer, before doing any work:
110	
111	```
112	Picking up: <repo>
113	Last session: <date>, <mac|windows>
114	Where things stand: <two lines from STATUS.md Current state>
115	Blocked on: <open questions, or "nothing">
116	Next: <top one or two from STATUS.md Next>
117	```
118	
119	Stop there and wait for Eric to confirm or redirect. Do not start the next task off the back of STATUS.md on your own — it records where work stopped, not what he wants to do this morning.
120	
121	## Do not
122	
123	- Do not `rm` anything. Move to a `_to_delete` or `_OLD_*` folder if something must get out of the way.
124	- Do not rebase or force-push.
125	- Do not push DexaProject or any repo whose CLAUDE.md says its data must stay local.

   non-ASCII character (an em-dash becomes `ΓÇö`) and adds a UTF-8 BOM, so the
   saved copy is corrupt and every later diff shows a phantom first-line change.

   - PowerShell: `git checkout --theirs -- <f>; Move-Item <f> <f>.from-mac; git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - bash: `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-mac && git checkout --ours -- <f>`

   Never run `git add -A` while `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists — it stages the
   conflict markers themselves and commits a broken file. Stage only the named
   paths you just resolved.
4. `git push`.
5. Missing locally: `gh repo clone erash11/<name> DEV/<name>`.
6. No remote: `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

Windows note: line-ending noise (`LF will be replaced by CRLF`) is normal. If a merge refuses to start because of phantom modifications, run `git add --renormalize .` and commit before merging.

`pgrep -fl git` (or `Get-Process git`) first. If no git is running and the

---
name: closeout
description: >-
  End-of-session sign-off ritual. Sweeps loose ends, commits and pushes what needs it,
  verifies memory capture, writes a cross-harness handoff, and reports "clear to sign
  off" or what's still open. Use when the user says "/closeout", "any loose ends?", "am
  I good to sign off?", "close out for the night", "closing out", "goodnight", "wrap up
  for the day", or asks for a system health check before leaving. Do not use at the
  start of a session (use startup) or for a standalone automation health check (use
  claude-stack-doctor).
---

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute; it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included), then `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

from pathlib import Path

import cards

STATUS = """# STATUS

## Done
- 2026-09-14: **Prioritization system shipped.** Design in `docs/x.md`.
  - sub detail
- 2026-10-03: Org step 1 done.
- 2026-10-03: Org step 2 done, `portfolio.json` backfilled.

## Next
- **Build the PM system.** Start at step 1.
- second thing

## Open questions
- 2026-12-01: a dated question that is not progress

## Gotchas
- 2027-01-01: a dated gotcha that is not progress
"""


class TestParseStatus(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_stands_is_the_newest_dated_entry_last_one_wins_a_tie(self):
        got = cards.parse_status(STATUS)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands_date"], "2026-10-03")
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "Org step 2 done, portfolio.json backfilled.")

    def test_next_is_the_first_item_with_markdown_stripped(self):
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(STATUS)["next"], "Build the PM system. Start at step 1.")

    def test_current_state_section_counts_as_progress(self):
        text = "## Current state\n- 2026-09-01: older\n- 2026-09-20: newer\n\n## Next\n-\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-09-20", "newer"))

    def test_an_empty_next_is_none(self):
        self.assertIsNone(cards.parse_status("## Next\n-\n\n## Open questions\n- x\n")["next"])

    def test_dated_headings_and_bold_dates_count(self):
        text = "## 2026-10-02 (Mac): heading entry\n\n- **2026-10-01 (Windows): bold entry.** more\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-10-02", "(Mac): heading entry"))

    def test_no_dates_and_no_next(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("# STATUS\n\nfree text\n")
        self.assertEqual(got, {"stands": None, "stands_date": None, "next": None})

    def test_wrapped_bullets_are_joined(self):
        text = "## Done\n- 2026-09-22: first half\n  second half.\n\n## Next\n- Rerun Phase 7\n  after the season.\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "first half second half.")
        self.assertEqual(got["next"], "Rerun Phase 7 after the season.")

    def test_struck_through_next_items_are_skipped(self):
        text = "## Next\n- ~~old thing~~ done 2026-10-01\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_a_subheading_inside_next_keeps_the_section(self):
        text = "## Next\n### This week\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_long_lines_are_clipped(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("## Next\n- " + "x" * 400 + "\n")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(got["next"]), cards.CLIP)
        self.assertTrue(got["next"].endswith("…"))


class TestBuildCards(unittest.TestCase):

        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dev = Path(self.tmp.name)
        (self.dev / "Repo" / "docs").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.dev / "Repo" / "docs" / "STATUS.md").write_text(STATUS, encoding="utf-8")
        self.reg = {"projects": [
            {"name": "Repo", "dev_folder": "Repo", "status": "active", "purpose": "p",

            {"name": "DriveOnly", "drive_folder": "01_PROJECTS/_STALLED/D", "status": "paused",

            {"name": "Gone", "dev_folder": "Repo", "status": "archived", "updates": []},
        ]}
        self.ledger = [
            {"root": "DEV", "path": "Repo/a.py", "when": "2026-10-02T09:00:00-05:00", "machine": "MAC"},
            {"root": "DEV", "path": "Repo/b.py", "when": "2026-10-03T15:00:00-05:00", "machine": "WIN"},

        ]

    def tearDown(self):

    def build(self):

    def test_no_charter_means_no_due(self):

    def test_card_carries_the_receiver_and_whether_one_is_needed(self):
        self.reg["projects"][0]["lane"] = "job"

        self.assertEqual((c["receiver"], c["receiver_needed"]), ("Chris Ruf", False))

    def test_a_started_row_carries_its_7_day_countdown(self):
        p = self.reg["projects"][0]

        self.assertEqual((c["clock_left"], c["clock_needs"]), (5, "a receiver and step 1 done"))

    def test_a_proved_or_exempt_row_has_no_countdown(self):

        self.assertIsNone(c["clock_left"])

    def test_retired_rows_get_no_card(self):
        self.assertNotIn("Gone", self.build())

import datetime
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import cards

STATUS = """# STATUS

## Done
- 2026-09-14: **Prioritization system shipped.** Design in `docs/x.md`.
  - sub detail
- 2026-10-03: Org step 1 done.
- 2026-10-03: Org step 2 done, `portfolio.json` backfilled.

## Next
- **Build the PM system.** Start at step 1.
- second thing

## Open questions
- 2026-12-01: a dated question that is not progress

## Gotchas
- 2027-01-01: a dated gotcha that is not progress
"""


class TestParseStatus(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_stands_is_the_newest_dated_entry_last_one_wins_a_tie(self):
        got = cards.parse_status(STATUS)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands_date"], "2026-10-03")
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "Org step 2 done, portfolio.json backfilled.")

    def test_next_is_the_first_item_with_markdown_stripped(self):
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(STATUS)["next"], "Build the PM system. Start at step 1.")

    def test_current_state_section_counts_as_progress(self):
        text = "## Current state\n- 2026-09-01: older\n- 2026-09-20: newer\n\n## Next\n-\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-09-20", "newer"))

    def test_an_empty_next_is_none(self):
        self.assertIsNone(cards.parse_status("## Next\n-\n\n## Open questions\n- x\n")["next"])

    def test_dated_headings_and_bold_dates_count(self):
        text = "## 2026-10-02 (Mac): heading entry\n\n- **2026-10-01 (Windows): bold entry.** more\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual((got["stands_date"], got["stands"]), ("2026-10-02", "(Mac): heading entry"))

    def test_no_dates_and_no_next(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("# STATUS\n\nfree text\n")
        self.assertEqual(got, {"stands": None, "stands_date": None, "next": None})

    def test_wrapped_bullets_are_joined(self):
        text = "## Done\n- 2026-09-22: first half\n  second half.\n\n## Next\n- Rerun Phase 7\n  after the season.\n"
        got = cards.parse_status(text)
        self.assertEqual(got["stands"], "first half second half.")
        self.assertEqual(got["next"], "Rerun Phase 7 after the season.")

    def test_struck_through_next_items_are_skipped(self):
        text = "## Next\n- ~~old thing~~ done 2026-10-01\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_a_subheading_inside_next_keeps_the_section(self):
        text = "## Next\n### This week\n- real thing\n"
        self.assertEqual(cards.parse_status(text)["next"], "real thing")

    def test_long_lines_are_clipped(self):
        got = cards.parse_status("## Next\n- " + "x" * 400 + "\n")
        self.assertLessEqual(len(got["next"]), cards.CLIP)
        self.assertTrue(got["next"].endswith("…"))


class TestBuildCards(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dev = Path(self.tmp.name)
        (self.dev / "Repo" / "docs").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.dev / "Repo" / "docs" / "STATUS.md").write_text(STATUS, encoding="utf-8")
        self.reg = {"projects": [
            {"name": "Repo", "dev_folder": "Repo", "status": "active", "purpose": "p",
             "next_action": "registry next", "updates": []},
            {"name": "DriveOnly", "drive_folder": "01_PROJECTS/_STALLED/D", "status": "paused",
             "next_action": "call Mike", "purpose": "",
             "updates": [{"date": "2026-09-30", "note": "newest"}, {"date": "2026-09-01", "note": "old"}]},
            {"name": "Thin", "dev_folder": "Thin", "status": "paused", "next_action": "", "updates": []},
            {"name": "Gone", "dev_folder": "Repo", "status": "archived", "updates": []},
        ]}
        self.ledger = [
            {"root": "DEV", "path": "Repo/a.py", "when": "2026-10-02T09:00:00-05:00", "machine": "MAC"},
            {"root": "DEV", "path": "Repo/b.py", "when": "2026-10-03T15:00:00-05:00", "machine": "WIN"},
            {"root": "DRIVE", "path": "01_PROJECTS/_STALLED/D/x.docx", "when": "2026-09-29T08:00:00-05:00",
             "machine": "WIN"},
        ]

    def tearDown(self):
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def build(self):
        return cards.build_cards(self.reg, self.dev, self.ledger)

    def test_repo_row_reads_status_and_newest_landed_entry(self):
        c = self.build()["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual(c["stands_date"], "2026-10-03")
        self.assertEqual(c["next"], "Build the PM system. Start at step 1.")
        self.assertEqual(c["next_from"], "status")
        self.assertEqual(c["touched"], "2026-10-03T15:00:00-05:00")
        self.assertEqual(c["touched_on"], "WIN")

    def test_drive_only_row_falls_back_to_the_registry(self):
        c = self.build()["DriveOnly"]
        self.assertEqual((c["next"], c["next_from"]), ("call Mike", "registry"))
        self.assertEqual((c["stands_date"], c["stands"]), ("2026-09-30", "newest"))
        self.assertEqual(c["touched"], "2026-09-29T08:00:00-05:00")

    def test_a_repo_with_no_status_falls_back_and_reports_nothing_touched(self):
        c = self.build()["Thin"]
        self.assertIsNone(c["next"])
        self.assertIsNone(c["stands"])
        self.assertIsNone(c["touched"])

    def test_due_is_the_earliest_undone_charter_date(self):
        self.reg["projects"][0]["charter"] = {"finish_by": "2026-12-01", "steps": [
            {"name": "one", "due": "2026-09-18", "done": "2026-09-17"},
            {"name": "two", "due": "2026-10-20", "done": None},
            {"name": "three", "due": "2026-10-10", "done": None}]}
        c = self.build()["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual((c["due"], c["due_what"]), ("2026-10-10", "three"))

    def test_finish_by_counts_when_every_step_is_done(self):
        self.reg["projects"][0]["charter"] = {"finish_by": "2026-12-01", "steps": [
            {"name": "one", "due": "2026-09-18", "done": "2026-09-17"}]}
        c = self.build()["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual((c["due"], c["due_what"]), ("2026-12-01", "finish by"))

    def test_no_charter_means_no_due(self):
        self.assertIsNone(self.build()["Repo"]["due"])

    def test_card_carries_the_receiver_and_whether_one_is_needed(self):
        self.reg["projects"][0]["lane"] = "job"
        c = self.build()["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual((c["receiver"], c["receiver_needed"]), ("", True))
        self.reg["projects"][0]["charter"] = {"receiver": "Chris Ruf", "steps": []}
        c = self.build()["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual((c["receiver"], c["receiver_needed"]), ("Chris Ruf", False))

    def test_a_started_row_carries_its_7_day_countdown(self):
        p = self.reg["projects"][0]
        p.update(lane="job", status="active", started="2026-10-01")
        c = cards.build_cards(self.reg, self.dev, self.ledger, today=datetime.date(2026, 10, 3))["Repo"]
        self.assertEqual((c["clock_left"], c["clock_needs"]), (5, "a receiver and step 1 done"))

    def test_a_proved_or_exempt_row_has_no_countdown(self):
        p = self.reg["projects"][0]
        p.update(lane="job", status="active", started="2026-10-01", seven_day_exempt=True)
        c = cards.build_cards(self.reg, self.dev, self.ledger, today=datetime.date(2026, 10, 3))["Repo"]
        self.assertIsNone(c["clock_left"])

    def test_touched_since_keeps_registry_projects_inside_the_window(self):
        names = cards.touched_since(self.reg, self.ledger + [

import datetime
import unittest

import portfolio
import sweep

TODAY = datetime.date(2026, 10, 9)


def reg():
    def row(name, lane="job", status="paused", **kw):
        return {"name": name, "lane": lane, "rank": 1, "status": status, "stage": "idea",
                "purpose": "p", "next_action": "", "dev_folder": name, "links": [], "updates": [], **kw}
    rows = [
        row("Old", updates=[{"date": "2026-01-05", "note": "x"}]),
        row("Older", curated_at="2025-11-01T00:00:00"),
        row("Touched"),                                   # in the ledger this month
        row("Kept", parked_until="2026-12-01"),           # kept parked, clock not up
        row("KeptExpired", parked_until="2026-10-01", updates=[{"date": "2026-03-01", "note": "y"}]),
        row("Live", status="active"),
        row("Gone", status="archived"),
    ]
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        r["rank"] = i + 1
    return {"meta": {"slate": {"cap": 1}}, "projects": rows, "ideas": [], "inbox": []}


LEDGER = [{"root": "DEV", "path": "Touched/a.py", "when": "2026-10-05T09:00:00-05:00"}]


class TestCandidates(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_paused_untouched_rows_oldest_first(self):
        names = [c["name"] for c in sweep.candidates(reg(), LEDGER, TODAY)]
        self.assertEqual(names, ["Older", "Old", "KeptExpired"])

    def test_the_weekly_limit_applies_but_the_count_does_not(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(sweep.candidates(reg(), LEDGER, TODAY, limit=2)), 2)
        self.assertEqual(sweep.pending_count(reg(), LEDGER, TODAY), 3)

    def test_a_row_with_no_date_at_all_sorts_first(self):
        d = reg()
        d["projects"].append({**d["projects"][0], "name": "Undated", "updates": [], "rank": 9})
        self.assertEqual(sweep.candidates(d, LEDGER, TODAY)[0]["name"], "Undated")


class TestDecide(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_keep_parks_for_90_days_and_logs_it(self):
        d = reg()
        sweep.decide(d, "Old", "keep", TODAY)
        row = [p for p in d["projects"] if p["name"] == "Old"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["parked_until"], "2027-01-07")
        self.assertIn("[sweep] kept parked", row["updates"][0]["note"])
        self.assertNotIn("Old", [c["name"] for c in sweep.candidates(d, LEDGER, TODAY)])

    def test_archive_retires_the_row(self):
        d = reg()
        sweep.decide(d, "Old", "archive", TODAY)
        row = [p for p in d["projects"] if p["name"] == "Old"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row["status"], "archived")
        self.assertIn("[sweep] archived", row["updates"][0]["note"])

    def test_revive_needs_a_next_step_and_a_receiver(self):
        d = reg()
        d["meta"]["slate"]["cap"] = 5
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(portfolio.RegistryError, "next step"):
            sweep.decide(d, "Old", "revive", TODAY, receiver="Kenny Boyd")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(portfolio.RegistryError, "receiver"):
            sweep.decide(d, "Old", "revive", TODAY, next_action="draft the outline")
        sweep.decide(d, "Old", "revive", TODAY, next_action="draft the outline", receiver="Kenny Boyd")
        row = [p for p in d["projects"] if p["name"] == "Old"][0]
        self.assertEqual((row["status"], row["receiver"], row["next_action"], row["started"]),
                         ("active", "Kenny Boyd", "draft the outline", "2026-10-09"))
        self.assertNotIn("parked_until", row)

    def test_revive_respects_the_slate_cap(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(portfolio.RegistryError, "slate is full"):
            sweep.decide(reg(), "Old", "revive", TODAY, next_action="x", receiver="Kenny Boyd")

    def test_a_knowledge_row_revives_without_a_receiver(self):
        d = reg()
        d["projects"][0]["lane"] = "knowledge"
        sweep.decide(d, "Old", "revive", TODAY, next_action="x")

    def test_only_paused_rows_are_swept(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(portfolio.RegistryError, "paused"):
            sweep.decide(reg(), "Live", "keep", TODAY)

    def test_unknown_decision(self):
        with self.assertRaises(portfolio.RegistryError):
            sweep.decide(reg(), "Old", "maybe", TODAY)


class TestParkedUntilValidation(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parked_until_must_be_a_date(self):
        d = reg()
        portfolio.validate(d)
        d["projects"][0]["parked_until"] = "soon"
        with self.assertRaises(portfolio.RegistryError):
            portfolio.validate(d)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""The Friday sweep: paused rows that went quiet get a decision (PM design Decision 6).

weekly-review puts up to 10 paused rows untouched for 30+ days to Eric, oldest first:

  revive   back on the board with a next step and (job/side/tool) a receiver; the slate
           cap and the 7-day clock apply, same path as the board's Start
  keep     stays paused; `parked_until` = today + 90 days takes it out of the sweep
  archive  retired

Undecided rows come back next week. "Untouched" means no landed-ledger entry, which
keeps 30 days, so a row in the ledger was touched within the window. Rows never seen
by the ledger are ordered by the newest date the registry has for them.

    python portfolio.py sweep [--limit 10] [--json]
    python portfolio.py sweep-decide <name> revive|keep|archive [--next-action ..] [--receiver ..]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt

import board_ops
import cards
import landed
import portfolio
from portfolio import RegistryError

LIMIT = 10
KEEP_DAYS = 90
DECISIONS = ("revive", "keep", "archive")


def _last_known(p: dict) -> str:
    """Newest date the registry holds for a row ('' if none): updates, curation, start."""
    dates = [u.get("date") or "" for u in p.get("updates", [])]
    dates += [(p.get("curated_at") or "")[:10], p.get("started") or ""]
    return max(dates, default="")


def _eligible(data: dict, ledger: list[dict], today: _dt.date) -> list[dict]:
    touched = set(cards.last_touched(data, ledger))
    out = []
    for p in data.get("projects", []):
        if p.get("status") != "paused" or p["name"] in touched:
            continue
        if (p.get("parked_until") or "") > today.isoformat():
            continue
        out.append({"name": p["name"], "lane": p.get("lane"), "last_known": _last_known(p),
                    "purpose": p.get("purpose", ""), "next_action": p.get("next_action", ""),
                    "receiver": portfolio.receiver_of(p)})
    return sorted(out, key=lambda c: (c["last_known"], c["name"]))


def candidates(data: dict, ledger: list[dict], today: _dt.date, limit: int = LIMIT) -> list[dict]:
    """This week's sweep: the `limit` oldest paused rows untouched in the ledger window."""
    return _eligible(data, ledger, today)[:limit]


def pending_count(data: dict, ledger: list[dict], today: _dt.date) -> int:
    """Every paused row awaiting a decision (the board header's nudge)."""
    return len(_eligible(data, ledger, today))


def decide(data: dict, name: str, decision: str, today: _dt.date, *,
           next_action: str | None = None, receiver: str | None = None) -> dict:
    if decision not in DECISIONS:
        raise RegistryError(f"decision must be one of {', '.join(DECISIONS)}")
    row = board_ops.find(data, name)
    if row.get("status") != "paused":
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: only paused rows are swept (it is {row.get('status')})")
    day = today.isoformat()
    if decision == "keep":
        until = (today + _dt.timedelta(days=KEEP_DAYS)).isoformat()
        row["parked_until"] = until
        row.setdefault("updates", []).insert(0, {"date": day, "note": f"[sweep] kept parked until {until}"})
        return row
    if decision == "archive":
        board_ops.patch_project(data, name, status="archived", note="[sweep] archived", today=day)
        return row
    # revive: Decision 6 says back on the board WITH a next step and a receiver
    if not ((next_action or "").strip() or (row.get("next_action") or "").strip()):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: revive needs a next step (--next-action)")
    if (row.get("lane") in portfolio.RECEIVER_LANES and not (receiver or "").strip()
            and not portfolio.receiver_of(row)):
        raise RegistryError(f"{name}: revive needs a receiver (--receiver '<who>' or 'me: <why>')")
    board_ops.patch_project(data, name, status="active", next_action=next_action,
                            receiver=receiver, note="[sweep] revived", today=day)
    row.pop("parked_until", None)
    return row


def format_report(rows: list[dict], pending: int) -> str:
    lines = [f"sweep: {len(rows)} of {pending} paused rows awaiting a decision (oldest first)"]
    for c in rows:
        who = f" · for {c['receiver']}" if c["receiver"] else ""
        lines.append(f"  {c['name']}  [{c['lane']}{who}] last known {c['last_known'] or 'never'}")
        if c["purpose"]:
            lines.append(f"      {c['purpose'][:110]}")
    return "\n".join(lines)

## Step 4b — Friday sweep (paused projects that went quiet)

PM system design Decision 6: paused projects untouched for 30+ days get a decision, 10 a week, oldest first, so the paused backlog clears instead of growing. Run:

```
python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py sweep
```

- **keep**: stays paused; out of the sweep for 90 days.
- **archive**: retired.

(decided 2026-10-03; built the same day, stages 1–9).

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Users

Eric Rash, Baylor's Director of Applied Performance — the sole user. Opens the
dashboard from a Chrome new tab on a work laptop and from the published
Artifact URL on his phone, usually first thing in the morning or between
meetings. The job to be done: answer "what do I touch today?" in one glance,
across two very different kinds of work (job deliverables with deadlines, and
side projects that are fun and value-adding but historically die on paper
scraps).

## Product Purpose

A personal portfolio dashboard that keeps every project and idea in one
registry (`portfolio.json`) and pushes the current front burner at Eric
instead of waiting to be opened. Success = the out-of-sight-out-of-mind
failure mode is gone: ideas get captured in seconds from any Claude session,
staleness is visible before it becomes abandonment, and shipping feeds the
SecondBrain via /harvest.

## Positioning

Unlike a todo app or generic kanban, every surface (published Artifact,
session-start pulse, morning briefing lead, daily re-render) is a render of
one registry file, so no two surfaces can disagree; and progress is partly
*earned automatically* — DEV folder activity heuristics and plan-checkbox
counting update the picture with zero manual upkeep.

## Operating Context

- Updated through the `/project` skill (idea / update / rank / promote /
  stage) in any Claude Code session; every mutation re-renders and
  republishes.
- Re-rendered daily by the KeystoneOS morning cadence before the unified
  snapshot; `pulse.md` opens every Claude session and leads the morning
  briefing.
- Two hand-ranked lanes: `job` (SPA presentation, NCAA doc, tech vetting,
  OKRs, Ask the Library) and `side` (morning briefing, TSSHB skills,
  curriculum). Claude flags staleness but never reorders ranks.
- Six-stage dev ladder (idea → grilled → spec → planned → building →
  shipped) maps to both the Matt Pocock flow and the superpowers
  brainstorm→spec→plan flow; `shipped` hands off to /harvest.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Single self-contained HTML file (inline CSS only) — it must render under
  the Artifact strict CSP and double as a local Chrome new-tab page.
- Generator is stdlib-only Python 3.14 (`render.py`), interpreter at
  `C:\Users\eric_rash\AppData\Local\Python\bin\python.exe`; tests must stay
  green (`python -m unittest discover -s tests`).
- Registry is the single source of truth; `dashboard.html` is never edited
  by hand. `render_pulse` output format is load-bearing (max 3 lines,
  consumed by snapshot/briefing wiring).
- Test suite pins visible strings ("⚠ Nd untouched", "Plan: X/Y tasks",
  "<stage> N/6", "/project stage") — copy changes must update tests.
- Phase 2 (deliberately deferred): session-end hook, reMarkable idea sweep.

## Evidence on Hand

Real data only: the seeded registry (8 live projects), live DEV activity
heuristics, and real plan-doc checkbox counts. Nothing on the dashboard is
ever fabricated; empty states teach instead of filling.

## Product Principles

1. **Push, don't pull.** Every design decision optimizes for the glance that
   happens anyway (new tab, session start), not for a visit Eric must choose.
2. **One registry, many renders.** Any feature that could let two surfaces
   disagree is wrong by construction.
3. **The next action is the headline.** Project names, metadata, and history
   are subordinate to "what do I do next."
4. **Claude proposes, Eric decides.** Ranks and stages are curated claims;
   automation supplies evidence (activity, checkboxes, drift flags), never
   silent changes.
5. **Capture must cost ≤10 seconds** from wherever the idea strikes, or it
   dies on paper again.

```
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-status "<name>" active|paused|done --note "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-receiver "<name>" "<who, or me: why>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" slate-check
python "<project-triage-repo>/board.py" --background

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.

  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.

  Start/Park/Done: a start over the slate cap is refused, and a start begins
  the 7-day clock.

  rules; exit 0 means a hand-edit is structurally valid.

  and prints its URL.

  mutation to `portfolio.json`. Stop and surface the message verbatim.

Read `portfolio.json`, show the lane's active projects with their current

only apply the order the user gives you. Rewrite the `rank` fields directly
with the Edit tool, then validate with `slate-check` (exit 0 = valid).

Ask which lane (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`) and for a

once: "Want me to run /harvest on <name> to distill it into your SecondBrain
and log the shipped artifact?" On yes, invoke the `harvest` skill for that
project.

Run `board.py --background` and give the URL, then show `slate-check` output
in chat.

changed in one line. Registry edits are committed by closeout as

- On any `[error] ...` output from the CLI: stop immediately and show the
  error verbatim.
- `portfolio.json` is the single source of truth; tasks live in each repo's
  `docs/STATUS.md`, which the board reads and never writes.

# /project — portfolio registry skill

Drives the shipped `project-triage` CLI to capture ideas, log progress, and
keep the front-burner dashboard current. The registry (`portfolio.json`) is
the single source of truth — never hand-edit `dashboard.html`.

## Paths

- Config: `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.windows.json` on Windows; `config.macos.json` on macOS
- Repo: parent directory of `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- Interpreter: `python` on Windows; `python3` on macOS
- Registry: `portfolio_json` in the selected platform config
- CLI entry points: `portfolio.py` (mutations), `render.py` (render)
- Generated: `dashboard.html`, `pulse.md` (both written next to the scripts;
  do not edit by hand, they are regenerated every render)

## CLI contract (verbatim — do not alter flags)

```
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<source>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" add-update "<name>" "<note>" --next-action "<optional>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/portfolio.py" set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"
python "<project-triage-repo>/render.py"
python "<project-triage-repo>/render.py" --no-scan
```

- `add-idea` prints `idea captured (<N> in inbox)`.
- `add-update` prints `updated <name>` (name match is case-insensitive).
- `set-stage` prints `stage set: <name> → <stage>`. Valid stages, in ladder
  order: `idea grilled spec planned building shipped`.
- `render.py` (full scan) prints `wrote dashboard.html · wrote pulse.md · ...`.
- `render.py --no-scan` does the same but skips the DEV/ activity heuristics
  (fast; use it after any registry mutation, and to validate hand-edits).
- Any error path prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr and exits 2, with no
  mutation to `portfolio.json`. Stop and surface the message verbatim.

## Verbs

### `idea <pitch>`
Run `add-idea "<pitch>" --source "<conversation context, ≤8 words>"`. The
source should summarize where the idea came from (e.g. "chat about GPS
vendor gaps"), not just "chat". Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `update <name> <note>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` against the project names currently in the registry
(read `portfolio.json` first). If exactly one match, run `add-update "<name>"
"<note>"` (add `--next-action "<...>"` if the user gave one). If the match is
ambiguous or there's no close match, ask the user which project they mean
before running anything. Then do the render + republish ritual.

### `rank`
Read `portfolio.json`, show both lanes' active projects with their current
`rank` values, and ask for the new order. Never reorder ranks yourself —
only apply the order the user gives you. Rewrite the `rank` fields directly
with the Edit tool, then validate by running `render.py --no-scan` (exit 0
means the edit is structurally valid). Then do the render + republish
ritual (this counts as the render step — no need to run render.py twice).

### `promote <idea>`
Ask which lane (`job` or `side`) and for a `next_action`. With the Edit
tool: set the matching idea's `status` to `promoted`, and append a new
project entry to that lane at the next free `rank` (max existing rank in
that lane + 1). Validate with `render.py --no-scan`, then do the render +
republish ritual.

### `stage <name> <stage>`
Fuzzy-match `<name>` like `update` does. Run `set-stage "<name>" "<stage>"`.
The dashboard auto-detects spec/plan docs (in the project's DEV folder under
`docs/specs`, `docs/plans`, or the `docs/superpowers/...` variants) and
renders plan-checkbox progress — the stage is your curated claim; drift
between the two shows on the card. Then do the render + republish ritual.

**Shipped → harvest handoff:** when the stage being set is `shipped`, after
the ritual offer once: "Want me to run /harvest on <name> to distill it into
your SecondBrain and log the shipped artifact?" On yes, invoke the `harvest`
skill for that project.

### bare `/project`
Do the render + republish ritual, then show the contents of `pulse.md` in
chat.

## Render + republish ritual (run after every mutation)

1. Run `render.py --no-scan` (fast path — the mutation verbs above already
   changed the registry; a full DEV/ scan isn't needed unless the user
   explicitly asks for a fresh scan).
2. Read `meta.artifact_url` from `portfolio.json`.
   - If non-empty: publish `dashboard.html` via the Artifact tool passing
     `url: <meta.artifact_url>`, `favicon: "🔥"`, `title: "Portfolio — Front
     Burner"`.
   - If empty: publish `dashboard.html` via the Artifact tool with
     `favicon: "🔥"`, `title: "Portfolio — Front Burner"` (no `url`). Take
     the returned URL, write it into `meta.artifact_url` with the Edit tool,
     then re-run `render.py --no-scan` and republish once more (now with
     `url` set) so the rendered page displays its own share URL.

## Rules

- Never reorder project ranks yourself — only apply the order the user
  gives you during `rank`.
- Never delete a project or idea without explicit confirmation.
- On any `[error] ...` output from the CLI: stop immediately, show the
  error verbatim, and do not proceed to render/publish.
- `portfolio.json` is the single source of truth. Never edit
  `dashboard.html` directly — it is fully regenerated by `render.py`.

# Runs the KeystoneOS morning packet + dashboard refresh. Called by the
# 'KeystoneOS Morning' scheduled task; safe to run manually.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$keystone = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "keystone.ps1"
$log = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "../outputs/morning/cadence.log"
try {
    & $keystone morning *>> $log
    & $keystone meeting-sync *>> $log
    # Portfolio dashboard daily re-render (project-triage/render.py). Runs
    # before snapshot so the snapshot's Front Burner section reflects today's
    # pulse, not yesterday's. Non-fatal: a render failure here must never
    # break the rest of the morning cadence.
    try {
        & "python3" "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/project-triage/render.py" 2>&1 |
            ForEach-Object { Add-Content $log "[portfolio] $_" }
    } catch {
        Add-Content $log "[portfolio] render failed: $_"
    }
    & $keystone snapshot *>> $log
    & $keystone dashboard *>> $log
    & $keystone cockpit *>> $log
    # Drift guard: cadence keeps the generated layer fresh, but nothing was
    # watching the hand-written layer go stale. Never fails the cadence.
    & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "os-freshness.ps1") *>> $log
    # Ritual guard: a skipped ritual leaves no error, only an absence. Both
    # rituals froze for 49 days before anything noticed.
    & (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "ritual-check.ps1") *>> $log
    Add-Content $log "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] cadence OK"
} catch {
    Add-Content $log "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] cadence FAILED: $_"
    exit 1
}

"""Restraint pass on board.html's <style> block: no uppercase, no tracking, system type."""
import re, sys
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(sys.argv[1])
html = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
a, b = html.index("<style>"), html.index("</style>")
css = html[a:b]
css = re.sub(r"text-transform:uppercase;?", "", css)
css = re.sub(r"letter-spacing:\.\d+em;?", "", css)
css = css.replace("--display:'Oswald','Arial Narrow',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;",
                  "--display:ui-sans-serif,system-ui,-apple-system,'Segoe UI',sans-serif;")
css = re.sub(r"\n  /\* Oswald, the display face.*?\n  @font-face\{[^}]*\}\n", "\n", css, flags=re.S)
# bold 700 display weights read as shouting once the face is the body face; settle at 600
css = css.replace("font:700 ", "font:600 ")
html = html[:a] + css + html[b:]
p.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
print("uppercase left:", css.count("uppercase"), "| Oswald left:", css.count("Oswald"))

Builds the project management system designed on 2026-10-03 (`docs/project-management-system-design.md`): all 9 build-outline stages, on the existing board (board.py / board.html), not a new app.

## Stages
1. **Live board**: `GET /api/changes` (registry stat + shown rows' STATUS mtimes); the page polls every 3 s and holds a reload while you type or drag.
2. **Resume cards** (`cards.py`): what / stands / next / touched, from STATUS.md, the registry and the landed ledger.
3. **Focus view + search**: active, paused-and-touched-14d, charter date within 14d; All rows; search across lanes. Drops keep hidden rows' order.
4. **Receivers** on job/side/tool rows; bare "me" refused; flag on the card.
5. **Start/Park/Done** through one slate-cap guard (`board_ops._guard_cap`), shared with the new `portfolio.py set-status`; 7-day countdown on cards.
6. **`board.py --background`** (one board per machine) behind `pm` (shell) and `/pm` (mod); dev-sync starts it after a clean pull.
7. **`portfolio.py card-check`** for closeout; header shows unpushed registry edits.
8. **Friday sweep** (`sweep.py`, `portfolio.py sweep` / `sweep-decide`, `parked_until`); header shows paused rows awaiting a decision.
9. **Retired** `render.py` / `dashboard.html` / `pulse.md`; the published Artifact carries a frozen banner.

Plus a styling restraint pass (neutral greys, system font, sentence case, gold for three things only) and a Windows fix: `save_registry` retries `os.replace` on WinError 5.

entries.name: SendUserFile
entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

content.text:
I built all nine stages of the PM system, on top of your existing board rather than as a new app, and toned the styling down. It's in draft PR #2 (https://github.com/erash11/project-triage/pull/2). None of it is live yet: `pm`, `/pm` and the ritual changes all run master's code until you merge.

**Your question:** I reused what you already had. That's the August board with its drag-and-drop, lanes, stages, inbox and undo, plus your registry, slate, 7-day rule and landed code. Everything new went into that same page. The styling had been overdone: green field everywhere, gold accents, and condensed all-caps type (`MATCHUPANALYSIS_FB2026`). So I did a restraint pass:
- **Colours:** neutral dark greys. Gold is kept for three things only: the active status, the #1 card's bar and the keyboard focus outline. Red is kept for flags that need action.
- **Type:** one plain system font in normal case, nothing smaller than 11.5px.
- **Usability:** the lane buttons no longer get cut off on an open card, and empty fields show a quiet dashed border instead of red.

The before and after screenshots are above. `DESIGN.md` now records this as the current style.

**What each stage added:**
1. **Live updates:** the page refreshes within about 3 seconds when you edit in the terminal, and doesn't redraw while you're typing or dragging.
2. **Resume cards:** each project shows where it stands, its next step, when it was last touched, and who it's for.
3. **Focus view:** shows active projects, paused ones touched in the last two weeks, and anything with a date in the next two weeks. "All rows" and search across lanes show everything else.
4. **Receivers:** job, side and tool projects name who the work is for. A bare "me" with no reason is refused.
5. **Start / Park / Done:** these buttons and the new `portfolio.py set-status` go through the same project-limit check. Starting a project begins its 7-day clock, which shows on the card.
6. **One board per machine:** `pm` in PowerShell (added to your profile) or `/pm` opens the running board or starts one. dev-sync starts it after pulling.
7. **closeout:** checks the card of every project touched that day and fixes the gaps. It commits board edits separately and prints the cards last.
8. **Friday sweep:** weekly-review puts paused projects untouched for 30+ days to a revive / keep parked 90 days / archive decision, 10 a week. 85 are pending now.
9. **Old dashboard retired:** `render.py`, `dashboard.html` and `pulse.md` are gone. The published dashboard page now carries a "frozen" banner. Because `pulse.md` is gone, the "Front Burner" section of the session-start snapshot no longer appears; that's intended.

**Checks:** the full test suite (309 tests) passed twice, after the restyle as well. Every stage was also tried in a headless browser against a copy of the live registry.

**Other repos:** these commits are local only. I haven't pushed them because they'd go straight to main.
- claude-skills: dev-sync, closeout, weekly-review and project skill changes
- dotclaude: the `/pm` mod
- KeystoneOS: drops the render step from the morning script
- DEV: router pages updated

**Steps for you:**
1. Review and merge PR #2.
2. Push `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.claude`, then run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` and restart Claude Code so `/pm` loads.
3. Open a new PowerShell and type `pm`.
4. On the Mac tonight, add `pm(){ python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/board.py --background "$@"; }` to `~/.zshrc`.

input.content:
# Using the project board — a working guide

For Eric. What the README lists, this shows in use. Read top to bottom once
(about 10 minutes), then do **"Your first 30 minutes"** at the end with real projects.

## The idea in four lines

- **The registry** (`portfolio.json`) is the one list of projects. Status, lane, stage,
  receiver, rank live there.
- **Each repo's `docs/STATUS.md`** holds the work itself: what happened (dated lines) and
  what's next. The board reads it and never writes it.
- **The board** is the front door: one card per project, live, editable.
- **Three rituals keep it true**: dev-sync opens it, closeout fixes the cards, the Friday
  review sweeps the paused pile.

The whole system exists so that six weeks from now you can look at a card and pick a
project back up without re-reading the repo.

## Your day with it

**Start.** `dev-sync` (or `/startup`) pulls everything and opens the board. If you skip
that, type `pm` in PowerShell or `/pm` in Claude Code. It reuses the board if one is
already running, so typing it again is harmless.

**During.** Keep the board open beside the terminal. Work happens in the terminal and the
repos; the board catches up within ~3 seconds of any change to the registry or a visible
project's STATUS.md. You don't refresh it. Use the board for the things it is good at:

| You want to… | On the board | Or in the terminal |
|---|---|---|
| See what's live | Focus view (default) | `portfolio.py slate-check` |
| Find anything | Search box (every lane, every status) | — |
| Pick a project up | Open card → **Start** | `portfolio.py set-status X active` |
| Put one down | Open card → **Park** | `portfolio.py set-status X paused` |
| Finish one | Open card → **Done** | `portfolio.py set-status X done` |
| Say who it's for | Open card → receiver field | `portfolio.py set-receiver X "Kenny Boyd"` |
| Re-prioritise | Drag within a column | — |
| Move a stage | Drag to another column | `portfolio.py set-stage X building` |
| Log a note | Open card → add update, Enter | `portfolio.py add-update X "note"` |
| Capture an idea | — | `portfolio.py add-idea "pitch"` or "new idea: …" to Claude |

**End.** Run `closeout`. It checks the card of every project you touched today, fixes the
gaps with you (below), commits board edits as `data: board edits <date>`, pushes, and
prints the cards last. Those printed cards are what the other machine, or you next month,
picks up from.

**Friday.** `weekly-review` now has a sweep: up to 10 paused projects that nobody has
touched for 30+ days, oldest first. For each you say **revive** (needs a next step and a
receiver), **keep** (parked; it leaves the sweep for 90 days) or **archive**. Anything you
skip comes back next week. 85 are waiting as of 2026-10-03, so about 8 Fridays clears it.

## Reading a card

```
 2  NCAA_BestPractices_Doc                    ← rank in the lane · name
    NCAA best practices document (Chris…)     ← what it is (registry purpose)
    for      Chris Ruf                        ← receiver
    stands   08-04 Confirmed as a separate…   ← newest dated line in STATUS (or registry)
    next     Collect source material and…     ← first item under STATUS ## Next
    touched  yesterday                        ← last file change, either machine
    ▪▪▫▫▫▫ idea 1/6               [paused]    ← stage · status
    7-day rule: 5 days left · needs step 1 done
    ⚠ Needs a receiver
```

- **"nothing on record"** on `stands` or `next` means the STATUS file is thin. That's the
  most common reason a card reads badly, and the fix is in the repo, not the board.
- **"touched"** comes from the landed ledger (30 days). Older means "not in the last month".
- **Flags** are the only red on the page. They mean an active project is missing a next
  step or a receiver.
- **Hover** the `next` line to see whether it came from STATUS or from the registry, and
  the `touched` line for the exact time and machine.

## What makes cards good (the part that's on you)

The board is only as good as STATUS.md. Two habits do almost all of it:

1. **A dated line for each session's progress**, under `## Done` or `## Current state`:
   ```
   - 2026-10-03: Week 5 EPA profile built; ASU game-day sheet sent to coaches.
   ```
   The card shows the newest one. A registry note dated today does *not* count for
   closeout; STATUS is the record.
2. **One concrete first item under `## Next`.** A command to run or a file to open, not a
   theme. "Run `pff_game_result.py --week 6` after PFF grades post" beats "keep going on
   matchups". Strike an item through (`~~done~~`) and the card skips to the next one.

## The rules that push back (on purpose)

- **Slate cap: 5 active job projects.** Start a sixth and the board refuses and says
  which five are active. Park one first. Other lanes are not capped.
- **7-day rule.** Starting a job, side or tool project starts a clock. Within 7 days it
  needs a receiver *and* step 1 done, or the next sync pauses it. The card counts down.
  Re-start it when there's something to show; the clock restarts.
- **Receivers.** Job, side and tool projects name who the output is for: a person, or
  `me: <why>` (a bare "me" is refused). system and knowledge projects are exempt.
- **Focus view hides things.** It shows active projects, paused ones touched in the last
  14 days, and anything with a charter date in the next 14 days. Each column says how many
  it hides. Click **Focus** to switch to **All rows**; the choice is remembered.

## Two machines

The registry travels by git. dev-sync pulls before the board starts; closeout commits and
pushes board edits. The header says **"N unpushed registry edits"** while there are any.
If you edit on Windows and skip closeout, then edit on the Mac, expect a JSON merge
conflict: run closeout before switching machines.

## When something's off

- **`pm` says the board did not start:** the log path is in the message. Usually a bad
  `portfolio.json` (it refuses to start on one; `portfolio.py slate-check` shows the error).
- **A change in the terminal didn't show up:** is the project in the current view (Focus,
  lane tab, search)? Polling only watches the STATUS files of cards on screen.
- **The unpushed-edits count is stale after a push:** it updates on the next registry
  change. Harmless.
- **Undo says "registry changed outside the board":** something else wrote the file since
  your last board edit. Undo refuses rather than wipe that change.

## Your first 30 minutes

Do these with real projects; each one teaches one part.

1. **Open it.** New PowerShell → `pm`. (After a Claude Code restart, `/pm` works too.)
2. **Focus vs All.** Note the job lane's card count, click **Focus** → **All rows**, look at
   the difference, switch back.
3. **Search.** Type `cfb` — the lane tabs show where the hits are.
4. **Fix a real gap.** Weekly_Matchups_2026 is active with "⚠ Needs a receiver". Open it,
   type a receiver (`me: in-season scouting I run`, or a coach's name), click away. The
   flag disappears.
5. **Watch it live.** In the terminal, add a dated line to
   `~/Desktop/DEV/Weekly_Matchups_2026/docs/STATUS.md` (or any visible project's), save,
   and watch its `stands` line change within a few seconds.
6. **Feel the cap.** Start a paused job project. (5 slots, 1 used, so it works.) Then Park
   it again.
7. **Preview tonight.** `python portfolio.py card-check` — the list closeout will walk you
   through: today's touched projects and their gaps.
8. **Preview Friday.** `python portfolio.py sweep` — the first 10 paused projects up for a
   decision. Look before Friday; you may already know the answers.

## Where to look next

- `README.md` — full CLI list and what the board can change.
- `docs/project-management-system-design.md` — why each rule exists, and what was rejected.
- `COMMANDS.md` (DEV root) — the desk reference across all projects.
