# project-triage — the project board

The one list of Eric's projects (`portfolio.json`, the **registry**) and the live
board that is its front door. Built to prevent one failure: losing the thread on a
project already known about. Design: `docs/project-management-system-design.md`
(decided 2026-10-03; built the same day, stages 1–9).

```
  terminal (portfolio.py, /project) ─┐                 ┌─ each repo's docs/STATUS.md
  board page (drag, Start/Park/Done) ─┼─→ portfolio.json ─┤
  closeout / weekly-review rituals ───┘                 └─ landed ledger (both machines)
                                            │
                                    board.py (127.0.0.1) ── polls every 3 s, re-renders
```

Tasks stay in each repo's `docs/STATUS.md`; the board reads them and never owns
them. The page edits registry fields only. The static `render.py` → `dashboard.html`
(and its published Artifact and `pulse.md`) retired on 2026-10-03.

## Starting the board

```
pm                      # PowerShell profile / ~/.zshrc function
/pm                     # in Claude Code (mod in ~/.claude/mods/pm)
python board.py --background
```

All three reuse the board already running on this machine (pid/port file in the temp
dir), or start one tied to the terminal and open it; it stops when that terminal
closes. `dev-sync` starts it after a clean `git pull` of this repo. `python board.py`
alone runs it in the foreground (Ctrl-C stops it).

The URL carries a per-run token; `/api/*` refuses requests without it, writes must be
same-origin, and it binds 127.0.0.1 only.

## What the board shows

- **Resume cards.** Each project: what it is (`purpose`), where it stands (newest
  dated STATUS entry), next step (first STATUS `## Next` item, else `next_action`),
  last touched (landed ledger, either machine), who it is for (receiver), the 7-day
  countdown while a start is unproven, and flags for a missing next step or receiver.
- **Focus view** (default): active rows, paused rows touched in the last 14 days, and
  rows with a charter date in the next 14 days. **All rows** turns it off; **search**
  covers every lane and badges the lane tabs. Columns say how many rows the view hides.
- **Live.** Terminal edits to the registry, or to a shown project's STATUS.md, appear
  within ~3 s. A change that lands while you type or drag waits until you finish.
- **Header nudges:** paused rows awaiting the Friday sweep; unpushed registry edits.

## What the board changes

- Columns are stages; tabs are lanes (`job`, `side`, `system`, `knowledge`, `tool`).
  Dragging sets the stage, the drop position sets priority (`rank` is recomputed).
- **Start / Park / Done** in the open card, the status pill, and the terminal's
  `portfolio.py set-status` all go through one function: a Start over the slate cap
  (`meta.slate.cap`, job lane) is refused with the reason, and a Start begins the
  7-day clock.
- Purpose, next action, receiver (a name, or `me: <why>`), notes, lane.
- Inbox: drag onto a stage to promote (lands active), onto Archive to retire.
- Undo reverses the last write unless something else wrote the registry since.

Every write validates against `portfolio.validate`, backs up to `portfolio.json.bak`,
and replaces the file atomically (retrying briefly on Windows file locks).

## CLI (`python portfolio.py <verb>`)

| Verb | What |
|---|---|
| `add-idea "<pitch>" --source ..` | capture to the inbox |
| `add-update <name> "<note>" [--next-action ..]` | log progress |
| `set-stage <name> <stage>` | move along the stage ladder |
| `set-status <name> <status> [--note ..]` | start / park / finish (slate cap + 7-day clock) |
| `set-receiver <name> "<who>"` | who the work is for |
| `card-check [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--project X]` | closeout: cards + gaps for projects touched today |
| `sweep` / `sweep-decide <name> revive\|keep\|archive` | the Friday sweep |
| `slate-check`, `seven-day [--apply]`, `week-report`, `mark-done` | slate rules |
| `crosswalk` | drift between the registry, DEV and Drive |

Any registry error prints `[error] <msg>` to stderr, exits 2, and never touches
`portfolio.json`. `landed.py scan|show` maintains the ledger of where files landed.

## Rituals that keep it true

- **closeout**: `card-check` for every project touched today; fixes gaps (a dated
  STATUS line, a Next item, a receiver) before pushing; commits registry edits alone as
  `data: board edits <date>`; prints the cards last.
- **weekly-review** (Friday): `sweep` puts up to 10 paused rows untouched 30+ days to a
  decision — revive, keep parked 90 days (`parked_until`), or archive.
- **dev-sync**: pulls this repo, then starts the board.

## Stage ladder

```
idea → grilled → spec → planned → building → shipped
```

Optional per row; rows backfilled on 2026-10-03 sit in an `unstaged` column until
dragged onto a stage.

content.text:
There was a README (a reference: every command and what the board does) and the design doc (why each rule exists), but nothing that teaches you how to use it day to day. So I wrote a guide for that: `docs/GUIDE.md`, in PR #3 (https://github.com/erash11/project-triage/pull/3). It's documentation only; say "merge it" and it lands. You can read it now at `project-triage/.claude/worktrees/pm-stage1-board-polling/docs/GUIDE.md`.

**What it covers:**
- **Your day:** `dev-sync` opens the board, or type `pm` / `/pm`. Work in the terminal while the board keeps itself current. `closeout` at the end fixes the cards and pushes.
- **Your Friday:** `weekly-review` asks you about 10 paused projects: revive, keep for 90 days, or archive.
- **Reading a card:** what each line means (for / stands / next / touched) and what the red flags and 7-day countdown are asking for.
- **What makes cards good:** two STATUS.md habits — a dated line per session (`- 2026-10-03: …`) and one concrete first item under `## Next`. This is the part that's on you; the board can't read what isn't written.
- **The rules that push back:** the 5-project job cap, the 7-day rule, receivers, and what the Focus view hides.
- **Troubleshooting:** the few things that look broken but aren't.

**The best way to onboard is the guide's last section, "Your first 30 minutes":** eight short steps on real projects. For example:
- Give Weekly_Matchups_2026 the receiver it's flagged for, and watch the flag disappear.
- Add a dated line to its STATUS.md and watch the card update within seconds.
- Start a paused job project to see how the slate cap behaves, then park it again.
- Preview tonight's `card-check` and Friday's `sweep`.

If you'd rather be walked through it live, I can run those steps with you in a session.

  ## MORNING START

  - **Suggests:** `/name-meetings` if generic titles appeared.
  - **Outputs:** `SecondBrain\Inbox\weekly-review\YYYY-MM-DD-review.md`, from `Templates/weekly-review.md`.
  - **Machine:** both.
  
  **forecast-capture** (`/forecast-capture`, "capture the forecast", "freeze this week's predictions", "did we capture this week")
  - **Purpose:** freeze the CFB Victory Model's pre-game forecasts for all 16 Big 12 teams before kickoff.
  - **Cadence:** "Run every Wednesday during the season." Wednesday comes after the model has taken in the weekend and before Thursday kickoffs. Seasonal (the football season).
  - **Calls:** `/Users/kristinarash/DEV/CFB_Victory_Model/scripts/weekly_run.sh`, which runs `uv run --with playwright python weekly_capture.py` and `compare_snapshots.py --all --archive`. Chrome must be visible (headed). About 10 minutes.
  - **Machine: Mac only.** "The Mac owns the weekly capture (decided 2026-09-23). On Windows, do not run it — stop and tell the user."
  - **Outputs:** `data/weekly_snapshots/<date>_<team>.csv`, `weekly_forecast_log.csv`, and `~/DEV/CFB_Forecast_Archive/<season>/`.
  
  **claude-stack-doctor (scheduled run):** weekly on Mondays at 10:30. See Maintenance.
  
  ## BIWEEKLY
  
  **status-report** (`/status-report`, "build my status report", "time for the Chris report", "biweekly update", "what do I send Chris this week")
  - **Purpose:** the Applied Performance report to Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf: about 270 words of plain email, a one-page memo PDF, and an internal record.

It also says "If any value starts with `C:\`, stop and fix the config", which conflicts with the current Windows config (every value there starts with `C:\`).

  **brain-audit** (`/brain-audit`, "audit my second brain", "score my brain", "is my second brain working")

  - **Purpose:** a read-only audit of project data: routing, indexes and freshness.

  - **Cadence:** on demand, "or when closeout/morning sessions should verify automation health." There is a scheduled weekly run on Mondays at 10:30: launchd `com.keystone.stackdoctor` on the Mac and the Task Scheduler task `KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` on Windows.

  - **Outputs:** read-only. A weekly failure appends to `.errors.log` and writes `scripts/last-weekly-run.log`.
  
  **doctor-plus** (`/doctor-plus`, "extended doctor", "then and now audit", "context checkup")
  - **Purpose:** runs `claude doctor`, then audits the workspace against six context-engineering shifts.
  - **Cadence:** on demand.
  - **Outputs:** a findings table. It changes nothing until approved.
  
  **backup** (`/backup`, "run the backup", "did the backup run", "I left the laptop off")
  - **Purpose:** run `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` on demand. It pushes the memory repos, copies state to Drive and the CRASHBOX SSD, and reindexes memsearch.
  - **Cadence:** the catch-up path when the Mac was shut at the scheduled time. The launchd job runs "at 21:00 daily."
  - **Machine: effectively Mac only.** It uses `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`; "It manages launchd, not Task Scheduler; the Windows original is parked at `daily-backup.ps1.win-orig`."
  - **Outputs:** `~/.claude/scripts/logs/backup-state.json`; archives and empties `.errors.log` when appropriate.

  - **Purpose:** find lessons in recent sessions that never got captured.
  - **Cadence:** on demand. The default window is 7 days for summaries and 14 days for raw records.
  - **Calls:** a subagent; `memsearch`; reads `claude-memory-compiler/reports/proposals-pending.md` first. Routes approved items through memory-write, capture-insight or write-a-skill.
  - **Outputs:** a checklist; updates to `proposals-pending.md`.

  - **Purpose:** find vault rot: stale seed notes, conflicting claims, duplicates.

  - **Purpose:** sort avoided decisions into four buckets, name 1–2 hidden reasons they are stuck, give 3 actions under 10 minutes each, then optionally decide in rounds and record each answer.

  interview-me ──► portfolio.py slate-check/add-update/mark-done ; optional meeting-sync→pp-fireflies,

  status-report ──► reads interview-me status-log, ledger (from harvest), portfolio.json,

  project ──► portfolio.py / board.py ; stage=shipped ──► offers harvest
  harvest ──► writes output/_ledger.md (Shipped source for status-report)
  meeting-prep ──► reads meeting-sync's "- project/<Name>" tags ; memsearch ; git log
  decision-audit ──► subagents ; portfolio.py ; memory-write
  session-miner / improve-system ──► proposals-pending.md ; memory-write / capture-insight / write-a-skill

  brain-audit ──► measure.sh ; hands off to claude-stack-doctor / improve-system
  aios-audit (KeystoneOS) ──► os-audit, brain-audit, improve-system, claude-stack-doctor, doctor-plus
  claude-stack-doctor ──► stack-check.ps1 + handoff-check.ps1 ; fixes point to /startup, /closeout, backup

  1. **interview-me Part 0b** hardcodes `python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.py`. That is the Mac path; on Windows the repo is at `Desktop\DEV\project-triage`.

# The ideal day — which skill, command and ritual, when

Eric's operating manual for the system built over the last year: every skill, mod,
script and scheduled job placed where it belongs in a day, a week and a semester.
`COMMANDS.md` is the reference for *how* to run each thing; this file is *when* and *why*.

Written 2026-10-03 from a full inventory of `~/.claude/skills`, the mods, hooks,
scheduled jobs and memory notes. Machine split since 2026-09-24: **Windows is the day
machine, the Mac is the evening machine.**

## Five rules that make the rest work

1. **Nothing nags you any more.** The 17:00 and Friday ritual nudges are off on both
   machines (Eric's call, 2026-10-03). This page and the status lines are the reminder.
2. **Type the slash command.** startup, closeout, interview-me, weekly-review and dev-sync
   are listed name-only, so "good morning" or "goodnight" may not trigger them. `/startup`
   and `/closeout` always do.
3. **One thread at a time, one session per project.** Pick one thing from where-was-i
   and work it; at most 5 active threads in global memory.
4. **STATUS.md is the record.** A dated line for what happened, one concrete first item
   under `## Next`. The board, where-was-i, closeout and the other machine all read it.
5. **Close out before you switch machines.** Unpushed work on one machine is the top
   cause of conflicts on the other.

## The day at a glance

| When | Where | Do | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sit down | Windows | `/startup` | Everything pulled, memory mirrored, board open, "Picking up" report |
| First 5 min | Windows | Read the status lines; `pm` board in Focus | What's live, what's flagged, what's due |
| Work blocks | Windows | One session per project; skills below as needed | The work |
| Before a meeting | Windows | `/meeting-prep <project>` | One-screen readiness brief |
| After meetings | Windows | `/fireflies-intake` | Transcripts named, synced, tagged to projects |
| Something ships | either | stage → shipped, then `/harvest <project>` | Ledger row (the only source of "shipped") |
| ~16:45 | Windows | `/interview-me` (10–15 min) | Supervisor log + reflection notes |
| ~17:00 | Windows | `/closeout` | Cards true, everything pushed, "Clear to sign off" |
| Evening | Mac | `/startup` → Mac-only work → `/closeout` | Pulls the day in; evening work goes back out |
| 21:00 | Mac (auto) | Daily backup + memsearch reindex | Keep the Mac awake and CRASHBOX attached |

## Morning (Windows)

**1. Open Claude Code in `~/Desktop/DEV` and type `/startup`.** Before you type anything,
the SessionStart hooks have already injected your profile, working memory, any hook
errors and the KeystoneOS snapshot. `/startup` then runs **dev-sync**, which:

- pulls `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.claude/global-memory` (the only thing that
  carries memory between machines);
- syncs the mods, applies the **7-day rule** (pauses unproven starts), refreshes the Codex
  skill copies, and mirrors project memory between the Mac and Windows folders;
- snapshots, pulls and pushes every DEV repo, keeping both sides of any conflict as
  `.from-mac` / `.from-windows`;
- **opens the project board** (if project-triage pulled clean);
- prints a six-line "Picking up: <repo>" report from its STATUS and latest handoff, and
  stops.

**2. Read the status lines (10 seconds).**
- `slate: …` (slate-status mod) — `/slate` lists anything DUE.
- Jobs and milvus (job-watch mod) — a red job or `.errors.log` line means run
  `/claude-stack-doctor` before anything else.
- Repo band — dirty, unpushed or behind repos. It will also stop you before the first edit
  in a repo that is behind origin.
- Next-steps band — three buttons from the newest handoff; a press fills the prompt.

**3. Pick one thread.** `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` lists every project's
first Next item, newest first. The board (`pm`, Focus view) shows the same projects as
cards, with receivers, flags and 7-day countdowns. Choose one. If nothing calls, the board's
flagged cards are the honest default.

**Monday extra:** claude-stack-doctor runs itself at 10:30; glance at `/jobs` after.
**Status-report Monday** (every other week): see Biweekly.

## Work blocks (Windows, the bulk of the day)

Open one Claude Code session in the project's repo. The repo's AGENTS.md routine
(`git pull`, read STATUS) runs first. Then reach for whatever the work needs:

| You're doing… | Use |
|---|---|
| A sport-science / RTP / S&C / workload question | Just ask — **sports-science-research-grounding** fires on topic and answers Zotero-first |
| Asking your books | `/library-advisor <domain> <question>` |
| Zotero housekeeping | `pp-zotero-research-library` ("search my Zotero", "what did I add this week") |
| Athlete load | `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` ("check ACWR"); on Windows read GPS/Perch/VALD from the Drive Parquet snapshots — the Mac owns the pulls (≈10:00 and 16:30) |
| A staff deck | `five-slides-generator` (Windows: PowerPoint) |
| The weekly paper | `/research-in-5` — build anywhere, export/publish on Windows |
| A coach-ready PDF | `html-to-pdf` |
| Power BI | `pbir-report-builder` |
| Explaining it to non-technical staff | `articulation-skill` |
| Understanding a codebase | `/graphify <path>` |
| UI work | `impeccable` |
| A new project | `/project idea …` first; once real, `new-project` scaffolds the repo + Drive folder |
| Starting / parking / finishing a project | Board card buttons, or `/project start|park|done <name>` |
| A thought worth keeping | `/capture-insight` (a story or lesson), `/ingest-resource` (an article, video, PDF), `/memory-write` ("remember this") |
| "Where did that save?" | `/where` (this session) or `/landed today` (everything, both machines) |
| Stuck on decisions | `/decision-audit` |
| Thinking a design through | `grill-with-ui` |

Keep the board open beside the terminal; it updates itself.

## Meetings

- **Before:** `/meeting-prep <project>` — what changed, what's open, and whether what was
  promised last time actually exists in the files. Minutes before, not days.
- **After:** `/fireflies-intake` — renames generic titles (name-meetings), syncs new
  transcripts into the vault (meeting-sync), tags each to a project, and reports what came
  in. Once a day after the last meeting is plenty; weekly-review also catches stragglers.

## When something ships

Set the stage to **shipped** (board drag, or `/project stage <name> shipped`); it offers
**`/harvest <project>`**. Say yes. The harvest writes the row in
`SecondBrain/output/_ledger.md` — the *only* place status-report takes "shipped" from — and
0–3 lesson articles. Skip it and the work is invisible in your report.

## End of the work day (Windows, ~16:45)

**1. `/interview-me` (10–15 minutes).**
- Part 0 (90 seconds): three factual questions → `Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This is
  the single best source for the biweekly report. An honest "nothing new" writes nothing;
  never backfill.
- Part 0b: did you work a project block? It logs `[block]` and marks charter steps done.
- Part 1: four reflection questions → the day's interview note and 0–3 permanent notes.

**2. `/closeout`.** One verdict for the session:
- git status across every repo; registry drift (crosswalk); 7-day rule.
- **Resume cards:** scans where files landed today, runs `portfolio.py card-check`, and
  fixes each gap with you — a dated STATUS line, a Next item, a receiver.
- Commits board edits alone as `data: board edits <date>`, then everything else; pushes all
  touched repos and the three config repos (global-memory even on a light day).
- Checks memory capture (errors log empty, today's transcript exists), harvests repo docs
  into memsearch, writes a handoff, updates STATUS.
- Ends with **"Clear to sign off"** and the cards. Item 1 of each STATUS Next is what
  where-was-i shows you tomorrow.

Automatic at 17:00: the Gmail digest (`DailyGmailDigest`).

## Evening (Mac)

1. `/startup` — pulls everything Windows pushed. (Mac `~/.zshrc` needs the `pm` function;
   see project-triage STATUS.)
2. Mac-only work:
   - **Wednesday, in season (to 2027-01-23):** `/forecast-capture` — freezes all 16 Big 12
     forecasts, ~10 minutes, Chrome visible. A missed week cannot be backfilled.
   - Anything that writes GPS, Perch or VALD data (the Mac is the sole writer).
   - Side projects.
3. `/closeout` before you close the lid.
4. **Leave the Mac awake at 21:00 with the CRASHBOX SSD attached.** The daily backup and the
   full memsearch reindex run then. launchd catches up after sleep but *not* after a
   shutdown — if you shut it down, run `/backup` next time you open it.

## Overnight (automatic)

| Time | Machine | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 21:00 | Mac | Daily backup (Drive + SSD) + memsearch reindex |
| 00:30 | Windows | AI session logs → Drive; repo docs → memory |
| 02:00 Sun | Windows | memsearch drain + recall eval |
| 02:30 Sun | Mac | Adjudicate |
| every session end | both | Session flush → daily log (memory compiler) + background reindex |

## The week

| Day | Do |
|---|---|
| Monday | Stack doctor runs 10:30 (auto) — check `/jobs`. Status-report weeks: see below. |
| Wednesday | `/forecast-capture` on the Mac (in season). |
| One fixed day | `/research-in-5` — pick a day and keep it; the series is weekly. |
| Friday | **`/weekly-review`**: syncs meetings, audits meeting names, reports registry drift, digests the week's transcripts and action items, writes the review note, and runs the **Friday sweep** — 10 quiet paused projects, each revive / keep 90 days / archive. 85 waiting on 2026-10-03 (≈8 Fridays). |

## Biweekly — the status report

**`/status-report`** on even fortnights from 2026-08-24: **10-05, 10-19, 11-02, 11-16,
11-30, 12-14** (the semester closes 12-18). It builds a ~270-word email, a one-page PDF and
an internal record for Chris Ruf (cc Kenny Boyd) and never sends anything. It is only as
good as the inputs the daily rituals left behind:

- interview-me status logs → "what happened" ("N of D days logged" shows the gaps);
- harvest ledger rows → "shipped";
- the registry's job lane → "in progress".

## Monthly and periodic

| When | Do |
|---|---|
| Monthly | `/brain-audit` (Mac) — second-brain score + two builds. `aios-audit` (in KeystoneOS) — skills, hooks, memory parity. |
| 2026-10-24 | Full OS audit is due. |
| When sessions pile up | `python ~/.claude/scripts/session-sweep.py`, then `claude rm <id>` for the SAFE ones (committed, pushed, in STATUS, >24 h old). |
| Every few weeks | `/session-miner` (lessons that never got captured), `/improve-system` (vault rot). |
| When the decision list grows | `/decision-audit`. |
| After a reading batch | `/library-review <domain>`; new books via `/ingest-book` (multi-session). |
| 2026-11-02 | Delete `~/DEV_archive_hold/2026-10-03` on both machines. |
| 2026-12-18 | Semester close: revisit the slate cap and 7-day rule with real data. |

## If… then…

| If… | Then |
|---|---|
| You don't know where you left off | `/startup`, then `where-was-i.py` |
| A scheduled job looks wrong | `/claude-stack-doctor` (read-only) |
| The laptop was off at backup time | `/backup` (Mac) |
| Memory seems missing | `/memory-write` recall ("did we already…?"); `memsearch search "<q>"` |
| You're about to switch machines | `/closeout` first, always |
| A project is drifting | Park it on the board, or let Friday's sweep decide |
| The board won't open | `pm` prints why; usually `portfolio.py slate-check` shows a bad registry |

Eric's operating manual for the system built over the last year: every skill, mod,
script and scheduled job placed where it belongs in a day, a week and a semester.
`COMMANDS.md` is the reference for *how* to run each thing; this file is *when* and *why*.

Written 2026-10-03 from a full inventory of `~/.claude/skills`, the mods, hooks,
scheduled jobs and memory notes. Machine split since 2026-09-24: **Windows is the day
machine, the Mac is the evening machine.**

## Five rules that make the rest work

1. **Nothing nags you any more.** The 17:00 and Friday ritual nudges are off on both
   machines (Eric's call, 2026-10-03). This page and the status lines are the reminder.
2. **Type the slash command.** startup, closeout, interview-me, weekly-review and dev-sync
   are listed name-only, so "good morning" or "goodnight" may not trigger them. `/startup`
   and `/closeout` always do.
3. **One thread at a time, one session per project.** Pick one thing from where-was-i
   and work it; at most 5 active threads in global memory.
4. **STATUS.md is the record.** A dated line for what happened, one concrete first item
   under `## Next`. The board, where-was-i, closeout and the other machine all read it.
5. **Close out before you switch machines.** Unpushed work on one machine is the top
   cause of conflicts on the other.

## The day at a glance

| When | Where | Do | What it gives you |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sit down | Windows | `/startup` | Everything pulled, memory mirrored, board open, "Picking up" report |
| First 5 min | Windows | Read the status lines; `pm` board in Focus | What's live, what's flagged, what's due |
| Work blocks | Windows | One session per project; skills below as needed | The work |
| Before a meeting | Windows | `/meeting-prep <project>` | One-screen readiness brief |
| After meetings | Windows | `/fireflies-intake` | Transcripts named, synced, tagged to projects |
| Something ships | either | stage → shipped, then `/harvest <project>` | Ledger row (the only source of "shipped") |
| ~16:45 | Windows | `/interview-me` (10–15 min) | Supervisor log + reflection notes |
| ~17:00 | Windows | `/closeout` | Cards true, everything pushed, "Clear to sign off" |
| Evening | Mac | `/startup` → Mac-only work → `/closeout` | Pulls the day in; evening work goes back out |
| 21:00 | Mac (auto) | Daily backup + memsearch reindex | Keep the Mac awake and CRASHBOX attached |

## Morning (Windows)

the SessionStart hooks have already injected your profile, working memory, any hook
errors and the KeystoneOS snapshot. `/startup` then runs **dev-sync**, which:

- pulls `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.claude/global-memory` (the only thing that
  carries memory between machines);
- syncs the mods, applies the **7-day rule** (pauses unproven starts), refreshes the Codex
  skill copies, and mirrors project memory between the Mac and Windows folders;
- snapshots, pulls and pushes every DEV repo, keeping both sides of any conflict as
  `.from-mac` / `.from-windows`;
- **opens the project board** (if project-triage pulled clean);
- prints a six-line "Picking up: <repo>" report from its STATUS and latest handoff, and
  stops.

- `slate: …` (slate-status mod) — `/slate` lists anything DUE.
- Jobs and milvus (job-watch mod) — a red job or `.errors.log` line means run
  `/claude-stack-doctor` before anything else.
- Repo band — dirty, unpushed or behind repos. It will also stop you before the first edit
  in a repo that is behind origin.
- Next-steps band — three buttons from the newest handoff; a press fills the prompt.

**3. Pick one thread.** `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` lists every project's
first Next item, newest first. The board (`pm`, Focus view) shows the same projects as

flagged cards are the honest default.

**Monday extra:** claude-stack-doctor runs itself at 10:30; glance at `/jobs` after.
**Status-report Monday** (every other week): see Biweekly.

## Work blocks (Windows, the bulk of the day)

Open one Claude Code session in the project's repo. The repo's AGENTS.md routine
(`git pull`, read STATUS) runs first. Then reach for whatever the work needs:

|---|---|
| A sport-science / RTP / S&C / workload question | Just ask — **sports-science-research-grounding** fires on topic and answers Zotero-first |
| Asking your books | `/library-advisor <domain> <question>` |
| Zotero housekeeping | `pp-zotero-research-library` ("search my Zotero", "what did I add this week") |
| Athlete load | `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` ("check ACWR"); on Windows read GPS/Perch/VALD from the Drive Parquet snapshots — the Mac owns the pulls (≈10:00 and 16:30) |
| A staff deck | `five-slides-generator` (Windows: PowerPoint) |
| The weekly paper | `/research-in-5` — build anywhere, export/publish on Windows |
| A coach-ready PDF | `html-to-pdf` |
| Power BI | `pbir-report-builder` |
| Explaining it to non-technical staff | `articulation-skill` |
| Understanding a codebase | `/graphify <path>` |
| UI work | `impeccable` |
| A new project | `/project idea …` first; once real, `new-project` scaffolds the repo + Drive folder |
| Starting / parking / finishing a project | Board card buttons, or `/project start|park|done <name>` |
| A thought worth keeping | `/capture-insight` (a story or lesson), `/ingest-resource` (an article, video, PDF), `/memory-write` ("remember this") |
| "Where did that save?" | `/where` (this session) or `/landed today` (everything, both machines) |
| Stuck on decisions | `/decision-audit` |
| Thinking a design through | `grill-with-ui` |

## Meetings

- **Before:** `/meeting-prep <project>` — what changed, what's open, and whether what was
  promised last time actually exists in the files. Minutes before, not days.
- **After:** `/fireflies-intake` — renames generic titles (name-meetings), syncs new
  transcripts into the vault (meeting-sync), tags each to a project, and reports what came
  in. Once a day after the last meeting is plenty; weekly-review also catches stragglers.

## When something ships

Set the stage to **shipped** (board drag, or `/project stage <name> shipped`); it offers
**`/harvest <project>`**. Say yes. The harvest writes the row in
`SecondBrain/output/_ledger.md` — the *only* place status-report takes "shipped" from — and
0–3 lesson articles. Skip it and the work is invisible in your report.

## End of the work day (Windows, ~16:45)

**1. `/interview-me` (10–15 minutes).**
- Part 0 (90 seconds): three factual questions → `Inbox/status-log/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This is
  the single best source for the biweekly report. An honest "nothing new" writes nothing;
  never backfill.
- Part 0b: did you work a project block? It logs `[block]` and marks charter steps done.
- Part 1: four reflection questions → the day's interview note and 0–3 permanent notes.

- git status across every repo; registry drift (crosswalk); 7-day rule.
- **Resume cards:** scans where files landed today, runs `portfolio.py card-check`, and
  fixes each gap with you — a dated STATUS line, a Next item, a receiver.
- Commits board edits alone as `data: board edits <date>`, then everything else; pushes all
  touched repos and the three config repos (global-memory even on a light day).
- Checks memory capture (errors log empty, today's transcript exists), harvests repo docs
  into memsearch, writes a handoff, updates STATUS.
- Ends with **"Clear to sign off"** and the cards. Item 1 of each STATUS Next is what
  where-was-i shows you tomorrow.

## Evening (Mac)

1. `/startup` — pulls everything Windows pushed. (Mac `~/.zshrc` needs the `pm` function;
   see project-triage STATUS.)
2. Mac-only work:
   - **Wednesday, in season (to 2027-01-23):** `/forecast-capture` — freezes all 16 Big 12
     forecasts, ~10 minutes, Chrome visible. A missed week cannot be backfilled.
   - Anything that writes GPS, Perch or VALD data (the Mac is the sole writer).
   - Side projects.

| 02:30 Sun | Mac | Adjudicate |

| Wednesday | `/forecast-capture` on the Mac (in season). |

| Friday | **`/weekly-review`**: syncs meetings, audits meeting names, reports registry drift, digests the week's transcripts and action items, writes the review note, and runs the **Friday sweep** — 10 quiet paused projects, each revive / keep 90 days / archive. 85 waiting on 2026-10-03 (≈8 Fridays). |

# ~/DEV — workspace map

Eric Rash — Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics. Sport science and
football analytics, plus the agent system that runs them.

This file is a **map, not a rulebook**. Behavior rules live in
`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Read only the index you need.

## Areas

| Area | Index | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Football | `FOOTBALL.md` | Game film, player analytics, CFB prediction. ~39k files — about two thirds of DEV. |
| Performance | `PERFORMANCE.md` | Athlete monitoring, testing, load, risk. GPS, force plate, VALD, DEXA, S2. |
| Research | `RESEARCH.md` | Literature, Zotero, book library, reading pipelines. |
| Platform | `PLATFORM.md` | KeystoneOS, dashboards, CLIs, scheduled jobs. |
| Program | `PROGRAM.md` | Staff reporting, curriculum, proposals, vetting, brand. |
| Personal | `PERSONAL.md` | Side projects. Not Baylor work. |
| Commands | `COMMANDS.md` | Desk reference: every report/project command Eric can run himself. |

## Elsewhere on disk

`~/DEV` in this file means the workspace root: `~/DEV` on the Mac,
`~/Desktop/DEV` on Windows. Paths that differ per machine are in `~/.claude/machine.md`.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `~/DEV/_ARCHIVE/` | Parked projects. Not a git repo, so the consolidation sweep skips it. Has its own `README.md`. |
| `~/DEV/_INBOX/` | Loose files from the `~/DEV` root. Own repo. |
| SecondBrain vault | Obsidian vault, ~850 notes. Own `CLAUDE.md`. Mac `~/SecondBrain`, Windows `~/Desktop/SecondBrain`. |
| `~/.claude/skills/` | ~45 skills (plugins add more) |
| `~/go/bin/` | ~8 custom CLIs built with `cli-printing-press` |
| `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/` | ~190 compiled articles |

## Layout rules

Full rules — grouping depth, the depth-2 discovery limit, and the gitignored-subtree
trap — live in project memory: `project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md`.

- 23 projects carry their own `CLAUDE.md`. Read it before working in one.

## Handling care

- `DexaProject/` holds identifiable health data. It lives on Google Drive, not in
  `~/DEV`, on **both** machines — one copy, reached by each machine's own path:
  - Mac: `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/DexaProject`
  - Windows: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\DexaProject`

  See `PERFORMANCE.md`.
  Never paste its contents into chat, an artifact, or an external service.

## Keeping this true

When a file moves or a new project starts, **update the router in the same
turn**. A stale pointer is worse than no pointer.

The counts above are approximate on purpose — they convey scale, not state, and
a `~` keeps ordinary growth from making this file wrong. Re-measure them only
when one is off by enough to change a decision. Counts last checked 2026-10-02.

Memory files named in these indexes (`project_*.md`, `user_*.md`) live in the
workspace's Tier A folder: Mac `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/`,
Windows `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV/memory/`. They auto-load
only when cwd is the workspace root itself — from inside a sub-project, open them by path.

Search everything with `memsearch search "<query>" --top-k 5`.

I've written `WORKFLOW.md` at the top of your DEV folder: the ideal day, week and semester across every skill, command and scheduled job. It's built from a full check of your 45 skills, 10 mods, hooks, scheduled jobs and cadence notes, not from memory. CLAUDE.md and COMMANDS.md now link to it. It's committed locally in the DEV repo (`031b5b6`) but not pushed, because that would go straight to main; your next closeout pushes it.

**The ideal day:**
- **Sit down (Windows):** type `/startup`. It pulls everything, applies the 7-day rule, mirrors memory, opens the board, and tells you where you left off. Spend ten seconds on the status lines, then pick one thread from `where-was-i.py` or the board.
- **Work blocks:** one Claude Code session per project. The guide has a table matching what you're doing to the right skill: research questions, books, Zotero, athlete load, decks, Research in 5, PDFs, capturing ideas and notes, "where did that save", and decisions you're stuck on.
- **Meetings:** `/meeting-prep <project>` before, `/fireflies-intake` after.
- **When something ships:** mark it shipped, then `/harvest`. Your status report only counts work as shipped if it's in the harvest ledger.
- **About 16:45:** `/interview-me`, then `/closeout`.
- **Evening (Mac):** `/startup`, then Mac-only work (forecast capture on Wednesdays in season, data writes, side projects), then `/closeout`. Leave the Mac awake at 21:00 with the backup SSD (CRASHBOX) plugged in, because that's when the backup runs.

**The longer rhythms:**
- **Weekly:** stack doctor runs itself Monday at 10:30. Forecast capture is Wednesday. `/weekly-review` on Friday includes the paused-project sweep.
- **Biweekly:** `/status-report` on 10-05, 10-19, 11-02, 11-16, 11-30 and 12-14. It's only as good as the interview logs and harvest entries the daily habits leave behind.
- **Monthly and one-off dates:** brain audit and AI-OS audit monthly; the OS audit on 10-24; the archive-folder delete on 11-02; and a review of the slate rules at semester close on 12-18.

**One thing the guide leads with:** nothing reminds you any more. The 17:00 and Friday nudges are off on both machines, by your choice on 10-03. Also, `/startup` and `/closeout` are the reliable way in; phrases like "good morning" or "goodnight" may not trigger those skills.

**Problems the research found (they're listed at the end of the guide):**
- `/interview-me` Part 0b uses a Mac-only path, so it fails on Windows.
- `/status-report` refuses Windows config paths, and its PDF check uses the Mac's Chrome.
- Two linked skills are empty folders (humanizer, session-handoff); `/research-in-5` and `/closeout` refer to them.
- A Mac-only `dcg` safety hook is back in your settings and errors on Windows.
- Some docs are out of date: a memory note and COMMANDS.md still describe the old nudge schedule and a 09:00 backup (it's 21:00).
- Two recent job runs failed: the 10-03 AI-sessions backup (killed) and the 09-28 stack doctor (terminated).

The first two would break your Windows day. I can fix them next if you want. I can also turn the guide into a one-page visual timeline you can keep open.

file.content:
`assets/one-pager.html` with the period's content. One page, always.

   **It is a printed memorandum, not a dashboard.** Single column, one serif family,
   letterspaced small-cap section heads, one green hairline. Never reintroduce status
   dots, badge or pill rows, bolded stat lines, progress bars, or a two-column grid —
   that vocabulary is what made the first version read as generated.

   **Measure before shipping**, don't eyeball it. Budget is **950px of content at 666px
   width**:

   ```bash
   python3 -c "s=open('<file>.html').read(); open('/tmp/probe.html','w').write(
     s.replace('</body>','<script>window.addEventListener(\"load\",()=>{document.title=
     \"H:\"+Math.round(document.body.getBoundingClientRect().height)})</script></body>'))"
   "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless --disable-gpu \
     --virtual-time-budget=3000 --window-size=666,1200 --dump-dom file:///tmp/probe.html \
     | grep -o '<title>H:[0-9]*'
   ```

   Then render: `--headless --disable-gpu --no-pdf-header-footer --print-to-pdf=<out>`.
   Over 950px, **cut prose** — never drop below 9.6pt. This gets printed and read by
   people who will not squint for you.
3. **`{vault_status_reports}/YYYY-MM-DD-email.txt`** — the email body as **plain text**,
   the file the user actually touches each cycle. Strip all markdown: no `**bold**`, no
   `-` bullets rendered as syntax. Use `•` or plain indentation, and spell section
   headers in caps (`SHIPPED`, `IN PROGRESS`). Outlook's compose window pastes markdown
   asterisks literally, and a supervisor email full of `**` reads as carelessness.
   Select-all-copy from this file should produce something sendable with zero cleanup.
4. **Also print the email text in the response** so the user can read it without opening
   a file — but the `.txt` is the artifact of record for sending.

name: vendored-skill-install
description: "Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different"

Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files, ~360 of
them) with `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
directories are symlinks into it:

- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → `~/.claude/skills/<name>` (absolute, hopping through
  the Claude symlink — verified on disk 2026-09-04. It does **not** point straight
  at `~/.agents/skills/`.)

Install with the CLI that owns that store when you can:

```bash
npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
```

**Trap: in Claude Code auto mode the CLI itself is blocked.** The permission
classifier denies `npx -y skills@latest add …` outright (hit 2026-09-04).
Hand-install is then the working route, and it is enough — the files plus the two
symlinks are all a harness needs:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/NAME
cp REPO/CAT/NAME/SKILL.md ~/.agents/skills/NAME/
cp -R REPO/CAT/NAME/scripts REPO/CAT/NAME/agents ~/.agents/skills/NAME/   # when present
chmod +x ~/.agents/skills/NAME/scripts/*.sh
ln -s ../../.agents/skills/NAME ~/.claude/skills/NAME
ln -s ~/.claude/skills/NAME ~/.codex/skills/NAME
```

Copy `agents/openai.yaml` too whenever the skill ships one — it is the
Codex-facing manifest, and dropping it leaves Codex with a half install.

**Trap: never put `rm -rf` in the install script.** The `dcg` PreToolUse guard
blocks the *entire* command on rule `core.filesystem:rm-rf-general`, even when the
target is a subfolder you just created yourself. Copy only what you want instead of
copy-then-delete. `dcg` also false-positives on a `>` inside a heredoc'd Python
script (rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`) — use the Edit tool for
that write rather than fighting the pattern.

**Trap: a hand-install is invisible to the ledger.** It gets no entry in
`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`, so `skills update` will never touch it.
`skillFolderHash` is not a plain sha1 of the files and is not worth
reverse-engineering — have Eric run the official `add` command himself behind a `!`
prefix to register it.

fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.

`KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (triggers 00:30, runs on wake if missed) can report Task Scheduler `FAIL(code=3221225786)` (0xC000013A, STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT — process killed, not a script error) even though the day's backup is fine. Cause: the git-push + robocopy phases finish in minutes, but the full memsearch reindex runs for hours; a laptop sleep/wake cycle mid-reindex kills the process, and the missed-start relaunch retries on each wake until one run completes (seen 2026-08-01: four killed starts 08:27–11:32, clean end 16:36).

**Why:** stack-doctor flags `task:KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` on the stale exit code; treating it as real rot wastes a foreground re-run.

**How to apply:** when this code appears, check `~\.claude\scripts\logs\daily-backup.log` for a same-day `===== daily-backup end: OK =====` and the script's own "Backup freshness" section. If both are clean, the failure is the sleep-kill signature — no fix needed; the code clears at the next completed scheduled run. Only escalate if no clean end exists for the day. content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

4	metadata:

10	
11	**Built 2026-08-31.** Closes ARMS gap 5. `~/DEV/CommandCentre/server.py`, served by
12	`com.keystone.commandcentre` (`RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`), own `DESIGN.md`.
13	
14	**<http://localhost:7373>** — one page answering "is anything broken?": agent
15	health, backup result, graph progress, logged failures, active projects, and
16	links to every generated report with its age.
17	
18	Design rules that must hold, each learned the hard way:
19	
20	- **Standard library only.** Python 3.14 here is PEP 668-managed, so any
21	  dependency means a venv to maintain forever. A read-only local page never
22	  earns that.
23	- **Rendered fresh per request.** Never cached, never regenerated on a timer. A
24	  page that can be stale is a page you stop believing — that is exactly why the
25	  on-demand `project-triage/dashboard.html` never became a front door.
26	- **A dashboard that contradicts the CLI is worse than no dashboard.** The file
27	  counter first used `total - len(done)` and disagreed with `gf_remaining.py` by
28	  13, because the done-list holds entries no longer in the corpus. It now does
29	  the same **set difference**, and the corpus selection is kept identical across
30	  `server.py`, `gf_gemini.py` and `gf_remaining.py`.
31	- **Judge a running service on its PID, not its last exit code.** A `KeepAlive`
32	  daemon carries the exit code of the instance that *died*, so a restart leaves a
33	  nonzero code behind permanently. `launchctl list`'s first column is the PID and
34	  the second is that stale status — reading the wrong column makes a healthy
35	  service look broken.
36	- **Live `launchctl` state is the truth**; `run-ledger.json` is shown but never
37	  allowed to claim a job succeeded. See [[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
38	- **Every source is optional** — a missing input renders "unknown", never a 500.
39	- **Bound to `127.0.0.1` only**, which is why it needs no auth. Do not change the
40	  bind address without adding one. Read-only on purpose: no buttons, so a stray
41	  browser tab cannot fire an agent. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` exists
42	  for the day buttons are wanted.
43	
44	**The threat to a localhost service is a web page you visit, not the network.**
45	Any site your browser opens can make requests to `127.0.0.1`, so binding to

  dependency means a venv to maintain forever. A read-only local page never
  earns that.

  page that can be stale is a page you stop believing — that is exactly why the
  on-demand `project-triage/dashboard.html` never became a front door.

  counter first used `total - len(done)` and disagreed with `gf_remaining.py` by
  13, because the done-list holds entries no longer in the corpus. It now does
  the same **set difference**, and the corpus selection is kept identical across
  `server.py`, `gf_gemini.py` and `gf_remaining.py`.
- **Judge a running service on its PID, not its last exit code.** A `KeepAlive`
  daemon carries the exit code of the instance that *died*, so a restart leaves a
  nonzero code behind permanently. `launchctl list`'s first column is the PID and
  the second is that stale status — reading the wrong column makes a healthy
  service look broken.
- **Live `launchctl` state is the truth**; `run-ledger.json` is shown but never
  allowed to claim a job succeeded. See [[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
- **Every source is optional** — a missing input renders "unknown", never a 500.
- **Bound to `127.0.0.1` only**, which is why it needs no auth. Do not change the
  bind address without adding one. Read-only on purpose: no buttons, so a stray
  browser tab cannot fire an agent. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` exists
  for the day buttons are wanted.

selection, the same skip gates, the same `GF_MAXBYTES` env override — including

<system-reminder>This memory is 9 days old. Memories are point-in-time observations, not live state — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>
1	---
2	name: backup-sync-system
3	description: "Nightly backup/sync architecture and its traps — two-writer root cause, manifest classification rules, Milvus is NOT in the memsearch path, dry-run can't verify writes"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 3db720f8-cca5-4aed-96cd-e7ac4a95ab2d
8	  modified: 2026-09-13T14:37:48.121Z
9	---
10	
11	**Current state (2026-09-03).** Two backup runs happen on most days, and the 09-02 entry was
12	right about that — but **not** because reconcile hard-codes the backup. The real mechanism,
13	traced 09-03:
14	
15	`keystone-reconcile.ps1` is a **generic make-up engine**. It has no mention of `daily-backup` at
16	all; it loops the registry at `DEV/KeystoneOS/data/jobs.json` and calls
17	`run-job.ps1 -Job <id> -Trigger reconcile -MadeUp` for any job with no success recorded today.
18	The `daily-backup` job is in that registry with `reconcile: true`, `graceMinutes: 60`,
19	`maxAttemptsPerDay: 2`, and `makeupWindow: 07:00-20:00`. Its `successProbe` greps today's
20	`daily-backup.log` for `daily-backup end: OK`. So:
21	
22	- **If no successful run is recorded by 07:00, reconcile replays it** → the ~07:00-07:10 run.
23	- **launchd `com.keystone.dailybackup` fires at 09:00 regardless** → the second run.
24	- **Run the backup by hand before 07:00 and reconcile skips it** ("already succeeded today").
25	  Confirmed 09-03: a 06:15 manual run logged `OK` at 06:25, and no 07:00 run happened.
26	
27	Registry inconsistency worth knowing: `jobs.json` records `schedule.at: "00:30"` while the live
28	plist fires at 09:00. The make-up window is what actually drives the 07:00 replay, so the stale
29	`at` has not bitten yet. Still true: `launchctl ... runs = 0` proves nothing — read the log.
30	Receipts cluster only on days CRASHBOX is attached: a mount gap, not a schedule gap.
31	
32	**"Scheduled runs cannot push" is NOT yet established — and the two contexts differ.** On
33	2026-09-03 the **09:00 launchd** run pushed `global-memory` cleanly and ended `OK (0 errors)`:
34	no `PUSH FAILED`, no `PUSH ERR`. But the **reconcile/`run-job.ps1`** context — which is where the
35	09-02 07:08 and 08-13 07:00 failures happened — **was not exercised that day**, because the manual
36	06:15 run pre-empted the replay. Do not read 09-03 as clearing the gap; it only clears launchd.
37	`daily-backup.ps1:74` no longer swallows the reason: the `Out-Null` was replaced 09-03 with
38	captured output that logs `REPO <name> : PUSH ERR | <text>` on failure only. **The error text will
39	only appear on a day nobody runs the backup by hand before 07:00.** Diagnose from that line rather
40	than assuming a credential gap. `daily-backup.err` is stale (last written 2026-08-06); never read
41	it as current. Manual remedy after a failed push is still `git -C <repo> push origin main` for
42	SecondBrain, `.claude/global-memory`, `.claude`.
43	
44	**SSD layout:** non-repo DEV dirs land in `DEV-nonrepo/`, **not** `DEV/` — there is no `DEV/`
45	on CRASHBOX (roots are `DEV-nonrepo/`, `DEV-repo-data/`, `DEV-working-tree/`, `claude/`,
46	`codex/`, `gemini/`, `SecondBrain/`, `_receipts/`). `._`-prefixed files beside every real file
47	are normal AppleDouble xattr sidecars on exFAT, not corruption or duplication.
48	
49	The nightly backup is `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (pwsh, launchd
50	`com.keystone.dailybackup`), driven by `~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`, logging to
51	`~/.claude/scripts/logs/daily-backup.log`. `~/.claude` is itself the `dotclaude` repo.
52	Workflow docs live in `~/DEV/Bucket` (`docs/SYSTEM-HEALTH-FINDINGS.md`,
53	`docs/AGENT-FIX-PROMPT.md`, `docs/FIX-STATUS-2026-08-14.md`).
54	
55	## The root cause behind most "divergence" symptoms — CLOSED 2026-08-14
56	
57	The retired **Windows box was still running `daily-backup.ps1` and pushing to the shared
58	repos** (SecondBrain, dotclaude, claude-skills, claude-global-memory). Two writers on one
59	set of repos manufactured `repo-diverged:SecondBrain` nightly. Identified by the
60	commit-message format `chore: daily backup sync YYYY-MM-DD [auto]`, generated at
61	`daily-backup.ps1:62`.
62	
63	**Retired 2026-08-14**: all 9 KeystoneOS/MorningBriefing scheduled tasks disabled (not
64	unregistered) on the Windows box; all four repos left at 0 ahead / 0 behind. It contributed
65	no unique history since 08-05 — only two append-only Windows failure logs, preserved
66	byte-identical to `~/Desktop/windows-retirement-2026-08-14/` on that machine and
67	deliberately **not** pushed (origin had already untracked `.memsearch-index.log` in
68	`a0e58c9`; committing would have undone a Mac-side decision).
69	
70	**Update 2026-09-10: the Windows laptop is ACTIVE again** (synced 9/9; both machines in use).
71	The retirement above is history, not current state. Unverified: whether its disabled
72	scheduled tasks were re-enabled. Before blaming a single writer for `repo-diverged`, check
73	the Windows task list and look for `[auto]` commits from it.
74	
75	Residual, by design — the box is meant to stay usable:
76	- **Session hooks still write.** `settings.json` `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hooks write
77	  `global-memory/transcripts/`, so interactive Claude Code use there re-dirties that repo.
78	  It cannot *diverge* it — nothing pushes on a schedule anymore. (That Stop hook is
79	  currently broken there anyway: `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on a mangled
80	  `C:\Program Files\Git\...\transcript-capture.js` path.)
81	- **`daily-backup.ps1` on Windows is still the macOS port** and still buggy. It is inert
82	  because the task is disabled, not because it was repaired.
83	- Three non-KeystoneOS tasks left enabled (`CFB-ForecastCaptureReminder`,
84	  `DailyGmailDigest`, `Refresh_All_Data`) — all operate under the Windows `~/Desktop/DEV`
85	  and touch none of the four repos.
86	
87	## Manifest classification — get this right, it routes athlete data
88	
89	`backup-manifest.json` is default-deny: any `~/DEV` dir absent from `paths[]` fails the
90	health check. Adding an entry requires a human class call:
91	
92	| class | destinations |
93	|---|---|
94	| `institutional` | `ssd`, `baylor` (+`github` if a repo) |
95	| `personal` | `ssd` (+`github` if a repo) |
96	
97	`isRepo: true` also sets `captureOrphans` and `captureWorkingTree` true and needs `remote`.
98	**Athlete data must never be classed `personal`** — `personal` skips the Baylor OneDrive
99	destination. `baylor` is `deprecated: true` and must never be a sole destination.
100	
101	## Traps that cost time
102	
103	- **Milvus is NOT in the memsearch path**, despite what `RESTORE.md` and the Bucket docs
104	  say. Indexing works with port 19530 closed and Docker not installed. Don't set it up.
105	- **`-DryRun` cannot verify a write path.** It passes `rsync -n`, which writes nothing. A
106	  snapshot that fails live will show `OK` in a dry run. Only a non-dry run is evidence.
107	- **Never size up a DriveFS destination with `du`.** It reports local cache/allocated
108	  blocks, not logical size — the `codex/sessions` mirror read as "47 MB of 289 MB" while
109	  actually holding 255 of 256 files, with a 35 MB file verified byte-identical by
110	  `stat -f%z` on both sides. Compare **file counts and per-file byte sizes**, never `du -sh`.
111	- **`snapshot:sessions` is a genuine hang** — not a size problem, not a lock, not a
112	  permission fault, and not slow enumeration. Three wrong theories died here in one
113	  session; see the evidence section below before forming a fourth. **Bounded 2026-08-14**
114	  by a watchdog in `Invoke-Rsync` (900s ceiling, hard SIGKILL, records `rsync-timeout`),
115	  committed as `8863a37`. That caps the symptom so the run reaches the SSD capture. The
116	  wedge itself is still unexplained.
117	- **Tier A memory is NOT in git.** `~/.claude/.gitignore` line 1 is `/*` (default-deny
118	  allowlist) and `projects/` is not allowlisted, so `projects/*/memory/*.md` has exactly
119	  two backup layers: the Drive SNAP of `~/.claude/projects`, and the SSD. With CRASHBOX
120	  unmounted that is a single copy. Nothing to "commit" there — it's by design.
121	- **`daily-backup.ps1` refuses to merge diverged repos by design** — that's correct
122	  behavior, not a bug. Reconcile by hand.
123	- **stack-doctor's cloud heartbeat** watches the newest per-run receipt
124	  (`_receipts/run-*.txt`). It used to watch `RESTORE.md`, which the job *copies*
125	  (`Copy-Item -Force`, line 411) rather than rewrites, so its mtime never advanced and the
126	  check cried `backup-cloud-stale (218h)` while DriveFS was healthy. Fixed 2026-08-14.
127	- **Untracked files block a fast-forward**, and plain `git stash` does not pick them up —
128	  needs `-u`, or rename them aside. Bit the documented SecondBrain fix.
129	- Reading exit codes through a pipe returns the *last* pipeline element's status, not the
130	  command's — see [[zsh-shell-traps]]. This produced two wrong readings in one
131	  session (`rsync ... | tail` and a stack-check run).
132	
133	## Standing state as of 2026-08-14
134	
135	Fixed: `Invoke-Rsync` false-OK guard, 6 manifest entries, SecondBrain reconciled (both
136	machines' briefings preserved, Mac copies renamed `*.mac-local.md`), stack-doctor cloud
137	heartbeat. Morning brief **retired** at Eric's request — `com.keystone.morningbriefing`
138	booted out + disabled, plist and `~/DEV/morning-briefing` retained, dropped from
139	stack-doctor's checked sets. `com.keystone.morning` is a *different* KeystoneOS cadence —
140	leave it alone.
141	
142	CRASHBOX SSD **reattached 2026-08-14 ~11:50** (`/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup`, 447 GB
143	free, writable) — first orphan/working-tree capture since migration due in the next
144	nightly. Bucket doc set committed + pushed (`ce94371`). Windows retired (above).

147	against running on a non-macOS host (it is the macOS port; `$IsMacOS` is PS6+, so
148	Windows PowerShell 5.1's undefined `$null` aborts too — intended), and `8863a37` adds the
149	`Invoke-Rsync` watchdog. Both are in dotclaude, so any machine pulling the repo inherits
150	them.
151	
152	Open: the `codex/sessions` wedge itself (bounded, not explained — see evidence below).
153	`.errors.log` retains 6 historical lines — clear the file once one clean nightly lands
154	with the Windows box off, not before.
155	
156	**Acceptance test — run 2026-08-14 15:48, mostly PASSED.** `repo-diverged:SecondBrain` and
157	`manifest-unmanaged` are both GONE (Windows retirement + manifest work confirmed). The
158	watchdog fired at 900s exactly as designed, killed the wedge, and the run *continued* —
