> **RETIRED 2026-10-03.** The CommandCentre repo was archived in the organization pass, and
> `~/DEV/project-triage/docs/inventory/mac_archive_pass.sh` stops and disables the
> `com.keystone.commandcentre` launchd agent on the Mac. The front door is now the live
> project board (`pm` in a shell, `/pm` in Claude Code; `project-triage/board.py`). The rules
> below (DNS-rebinding Host allowlist, fd-checked reads, "one number, one code path",
> judge a daemon by its PID) still apply to any local web service — the board follows them.

**Built 2026-08-31.** Closes ARMS gap 5. `~/DEV/CommandCentre/server.py`, served by
`com.keystone.commandcentre` (`RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`), own `DESIGN.md`.

**<http://localhost:7373>** — one page answering "is anything broken?": agent
health, backup result, graph progress, logged failures, active projects, and
links to every generated report with its age.

Design rules that must hold, each learned the hard way:

- **Standard library only.** Python 3.14 here is PEP 668-managed, so any
  dependency means a venv to maintain forever. A read-only local page never
  earns that.
- **Rendered fresh per request.** Never cached, never regenerated on a timer. A
  page that can be stale is a page you stop believing — that is exactly why the
  on-demand `project-triage/dashboard.html` never became a front door.
- **A dashboard that contradicts the CLI is worse than no dashboard.** The file
  counter first used `total - len(done)` and disagreed with `gf_remaining.py` by
  13, because the done-list holds entries no longer in the corpus. It now does
  the same **set difference**, and the corpus selection is kept identical across
  `server.py`, `gf_gemini.py` and `gf_remaining.py`.
- **Judge a running service on its PID, not its last exit code.** A `KeepAlive`
  daemon carries the exit code of the instance that *died*, so a restart leaves a
  nonzero code behind permanently. `launchctl list`'s first column is the PID and
  the second is that stale status — reading the wrong column makes a healthy
  service look broken.
- **Live `launchctl` state is the truth**; `run-ledger.json` is shown but never
  allowed to claim a job succeeded. See [[keystoneos-verification-habits]].
- **Every source is optional** — a missing input renders "unknown", never a 500.
- **Bound to `127.0.0.1` only**, which is why it needs no auth. Do not change the
  bind address without adding one. Read-only on purpose: no buttons, so a stray
  browser tab cannot fire an agent. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` exists
  for the day buttons are wanted.

**The threat to a localhost service is a web page you visit, not the network.**
Any site your browser opens can make requests to `127.0.0.1`, so binding to
loopback is not a security boundary on its own. **DNS rebinding** is the real
attack: the attacker's domain re-resolves to `127.0.0.1`, their JavaScript
becomes same-origin, and it reads everything. The defence is a **`Host` header
allowlist** — refuse any request whose Host is not a loopback name. Three review
rounds were needed to get the parsing right: compare IPv6 numerically (so
`[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]` is recognised), refuse a second `Host` header rather than
guess, strip exactly one trailing DNS dot, and validate the port range. Also
learned: **curl silently collapses duplicate headers** — prove that guard over a
raw socket.

**An allowlisted name is not an allowlisted file.** `Path.exists()` and
`read_bytes()` follow symlinks, so an exact-path allowlist still served
`/etc/hosts` when the target was swapped for a symlink. Confine the resolved
object too, then **read through the same descriptor you checked** (`O_NOFOLLOW`,
then compare the fd's `(st_dev, st_ino)` to the pre-check `lstat`) — checking a
path and reopening it by name is a check/use race. Close the fd in a `finally`
that catches every exception type, not just `OSError`.

**Any number shown in two places must be computed by identical code.** A page
that contradicts the CLI destroys trust in both. Three separate counters here
had to be aligned four times: set difference not arithmetic, the same corpus
selection, the same skip gates, the same `GF_MAXBYTES` env override — including
its "0 means no cap" convention — and the gate applied to a progress line's
numerator *and* denominator.

**Creating any new `~/DEV/<folder>` breaks the backup immediately** — the manifest
is default-deny, so `daily-backup` exits 1 until the folder is added to
`~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json`. Working as designed; just add the entry
in the same turn. The `class` field answers *who keeps this when you leave
Baylor* — `institutional` also copies to Baylor OneDrive ("lost when Baylor
access ends"), `personal` stays yours. See [[backup-sync-system]].

## The `/os` view — added 2026-09-01

A second face over the same sources: **<http://localhost:7373/os>** (page:
`CommandCentre/os.html`, data: `/api/state.json`). `/` is unchanged. Renders
routines, 148 skills, an artifact ring, Second Brain counts, health and projects.
Rationale lives in `DESIGN.md` → "The `/os` view". Backup: `server.py.bak-2026-09-01`.
Design study it came from (video frames + original spec): `CommandCentre/reference/rubric-agentic-os/`.

- **It is read-only, and that is not a gap to fill casually.** It shows which model
  and effort a skill *would* run at; it cannot run one. Run buttons and the model ×
  effort matrix were deliberately **not rendered** — dead controls are worse than
  none. `~/.claude/scripts/skill-button.sh` is the guarded write path for that day.
- **Never add a CORS header to `/api/state.json`, and never open `/os` as
  `file://`.** Same-origin is the only thing keeping the whole state object away
  from any site the browser has open. A `file://` page would need CORS to fetch it
  — that is the trap, not the fix.
- **`/open` allowlists ring files by identical string, recomputed per click** —
  same rule as `LINKS`, never a prefix or subtree test. The ring moves as files are
  written, so a click can 404 when it shifted underneath. That is the correct
  failure; widening the check is how a traversal gets in.
- **The ring must stay capped per folder and per project** (`RING_PER_DIR=2`,
  `RING_PER_PROJECT=6`). Uncapped "40 most recent" gave 22 of 40 from a single
  06:34 generated batch and buried every real deliverable. Verified: capped = 13
  projects.
- **`RING_EXCLUDE` keeps `COG_S2_Position_Reports` off the ring** — those filenames
  carry athlete names and the ring renders filenames as labels, so a glance would
  put named cognitive results on screen. Excluded from this view only.
  See [[s2-cognition-analysis]].
- **`SENSITIVE_PATHS` is module-level now**, shared by `src_graph` and the ring, so
  the graph count and the ring can never disagree about what is off-limits. Still
  must match `gf_gemini.py`.
- **Calendar and email cannot be on this page.** Both live behind MCP servers that
  only exist inside a Claude session; a background HTTP server cannot reach them.
  Caching them would break the never-stale rule the page is built on. They became
  System Health and Projects instead.
- `launchctl kickstart -k` leaves **exit `-15`** on the previous instance. Expected —
  judge it on the live PID, which `src_agents` already does.

- **To verify `/os` renders, use headless Chrome — not the claude-in-chrome
  extension.** The extension returns `Frame with ID 0 is showing error page` for
  `localhost:7373` on both `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`, while `curl` gets 200 and
  the server logs nothing. That is the extension's site-permission gate, **not** a
  server fault — do not go hunting for an IPv4/IPv6 bind bug (the server is
  IPv4-only by design, `server.py:878`, and that is not the cause). Working check:
  `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless \
  --disable-gpu --virtual-time-budget=6000 --screenshot=<out>.png \
  --window-size=1440,900 http://127.0.0.1:7373/os`
  **`--virtual-time-budget` is required** — without it the shot fires before the
  `/api/state.json` fetch resolves and every panel reads `LOADING`, which looks
  exactly like a broken board.

Related: [[graphify-semantic-extraction]], [[dev-layout-and-discovery]],
[[s2-cognition-analysis]]

I made the fixes and built the visual. Codex verified the fixes in two passes; the second was clean except one wording slip, now corrected. Everything is committed but not pushed (details at the end).

**Visual:** https://claude.ai/artifact/9kc2jSrPeGCWzyPAQDpcPt. It's the full workflow on one page: the day as a timeline with the phase you're in highlighted, the week with today marked, and the semester dates with the next one called out ("Oct 5 status report, in 2 days"). Every command is click-to-copy, it works on a phone, and it follows your light or dark setting. `WORKFLOW.md` links to it.

**Fixes:**
- **interview-me** now finds `portfolio.py` through your machine config, so it works on Windows.
- **status-report** no longer refuses Windows paths. Its page-height check is now one small script that runs on both machines. Codex caught that it would crash on curly quotes on Windows; I fixed that and confirmed it measures a test page exactly.
- **humanizer and session-handoff** were empty. I restored them from your `erash11/agent-skills` repo, and Codex confirmed the files match.
- **The Mac-only `dcg` hook** is removed from your settings again. This is the third time, because the Mac keeps putting it back (see Mac step below).
- **Stale docs:** COMMANDS.md and three memory notes now say nudges off, backup at 21:00, command centre retired.
- **The two flagged jobs:** I re-ran both by hand and both were clean. The 10-03 backup kill was a known sleep-related failure pattern, and the stack doctor finishes in under a minute.

**What Codex caught:**
- My first draft told you to reset `settings.json` on the Mac. That would have wiped any other unsaved setting along with the bad hook, so it now says to delete just that one entry.
- A few wording errors: who receives the status report, which repos carry memory, and the scheduled-job count.

**Codex itself was misconfigured.** `~/.codex/config.toml` sets the model to `gpt-6.1-sol`, which your ChatGPT login can't use, so every Codex call fails until it's changed. I worked around it with `gpt-6-astra` and didn't touch your config. Change that line to `gpt-6-sol` or `gpt-6-astra` and Codex works normally again.

**Your steps:**
- **Push:** these commits aren't pushed because they'd go straight to main: claude-skills (5), dotclaude (3), DEV root (3). Your next `/closeout` pushes them all.
- **On the Mac:**
  1. After pulling, run `git -C ~/.claude diff -- settings.json`.
  2. If the `/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/dcg` hook entry is there, delete only that entry, then commit.

  Without this, the next Mac closeout re-commits the hook.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). # Handoff 2026-10-03 (Windows, evening): PM system built, merged, documented

## What and why
Eric asked to build the project management system designed earlier today
(`docs/project-management-system-design.md`, 13 decisions) "until the project is done".
All 9 build-outline stages were built on the existing board (board.py/board.html), merged as
PR #2, then the board was restyled for restraint at Eric's request ("highly functional and
user-friendly; don't overdo colors or typography"). He then asked for an onboarding guide
(PR #3, `docs/GUIDE.md`) and a whole-setup workflow guide (`~/DEV/WORKFLOW.md` + visual
artifact), then fixes for the gaps that guide found, verified by Codex.

## Decisions (with reasons)
- Built on the existing board, not a new app (reuse; the drag/undo/token security was sound).
- "Keep parked" is a `parked_until` date field (queryable), not an updates note.
- "Untouched 30+ days" = no landed-ledger entry (the ledger keeps exactly 30 days).
- Focus view counts charter dates today..+14 only; overdue dates on paused rows don't pull
  them in (else the 5 slate charters Eric paused today would flood it).
- One slate-cap guard (`board_ops._guard_cap`) for page and terminal (`set-status`).
- A registry update dated today does not satisfy closeout's "STATUS entry dated today".
- Restyle: neutral greys, system font, sentence case; gold only for active status, #1 card
  bar, focus ring. DESIGN.md records it; the scorebug system is kept as history.
- Codex model in `~/.codex/config.toml` (`gpt-6.1-sol`) is not available to this account;
  ran with `-m gpt-6-astra` and left the config for Eric.

## Files
project-triage (merged in PR #2): `board.py`, `board.html`, `board_ops.py`, `cards.py` (new),
`sweep.py` (new), `portfolio.py`, `landed.py`, `seven_day.py`, `README.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,
`DESIGN.md`, tests (`test_cards.py`, `test_sweep.py` new; render tests removed),
`render.py` deleted. PR #3: `docs/GUIDE.md`, README pointer, this handoff, STATUS.
Other repos: claude-skills (dev-sync, closeout, weekly-review, project, interview-me,
status-report SKILL.md), dotclaude (`mods/pm/`, `mods/README.md`, `settings.json`, 3 Tier A
memory notes + index), KeystoneOS `scripts/morning-cadence.ps1`, DEV root `WORKFLOW.md`
(new), `COMMANDS.md`, `PLATFORM.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. Restored vendored skills
`~/.agents/skills/{humanizer,session-handoff}` (+ `~/.codex/skills` copies) from
erash11/agent-skills. Windows PowerShell profile: `pm` function. Published artifacts:
frozen dashboard banner (v24 of the old dashboard), workflow visual
https://claude.ai/artifact/9kc2jSrPeGCWzyPAQDpcPt.

## Next (most important first)
1. Merge PR #3.
2. `mods-sync.ps1`, restart Claude Code, try `/pm` and `pm`; walk GUIDE.md's 30 minutes.
3. Mac: `.zshrc` `pm` function; pull; `mods-sync.sh`; remove the hardcoded dcg hook from
   the Mac's `~/.claude/settings.json` if it is back (only that object); run
   `docs/inventory/mac_archive_pass.sh` then `--go` (stops the command centre agent).
4. Fix `~/.codex/config.toml` model line (`gpt-6-sol` or `gpt-6-astra`).
5. First Friday sweep 2026-10-09; status report 2026-10-05.

## Mid-flight / open
- `CATES/.claude/worktrees/cates-status-closeout/` is a leftover worktree from another
  session, untracked in CATES; not committed. Delete or gitignore it.
- Memory-compiler backlog note in `.errors.log` (run `compile.py` to catch up).
- Status-report PDF probe's Mac branch is untested until it runs there.

## Every slash command, by where it fits

All 47 of your own skills, the two KeystoneOS project skills and the mod commands, as of
2026-10-03. Plugin skills (superpowers, mattpocock, codex, etc.) are not listed — type `/`
in Claude Code to see those. **Bold** = part of the daily or weekly ritual. Commands marked
*auto* fire on their own when the topic comes up; you rarely type them.

### Start of day
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/startup`** | Sit-down entry point: runs dev-sync, then reports where you left off and stops. |
| `/dev-sync` | The engine behind /startup: pulls config, skills and memory; mirrors memory across machines; syncs every repo; opens the board. Also "is everything pushed?" |
| `/pm` | Opens the live project board (starts it if needed). Same as `pm` in a shell. |
| `/slate` | Lists what the slate check flags (cap, charters, due steps). |
| `/repos` | Repos that are dirty, unpushed or behind origin. |
| `/jobs` | Scheduled jobs, the errors log, memory-search health. |
| `/next-steps off\|on` | Turns the three suggested-next-prompt buttons off or on. |

### Projects
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/project` | The registry: `idea`, `update`, `start`/`park`/`done`, `stage`, `rank`, `promote`; bare `/project` opens the board. |
| `/new-project` | Scaffolds a new repo (AGENTS, CLAUDE, STATUS), its private GitHub repo and Drive folder. |
| `/decision-audit` | Sorts the decisions you've been avoiding, names why they're stuck, then decides them with you. |
| `/ISA` | Writes an "Ideal State Artifact": what *done* means for a project, as testable criteria. |
| `/grill-with-ui` | A design interview in a browser page, each question with a recommendation. |
| `/project-triage` | Older daily HTML dashboard of every DEV folder. Overlaps the board; use `/pm`. |

### Research and knowledge
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/sports-science-research-grounding` | *auto* — answers sport-science, RTP, S&C and workload questions from Zotero first, labels outside sources. |
| `/library-advisor <domain> <q>` | Answers only from your ingested books, with citations. |
| `/library-review <domain>` | Finds gaps in a book domain and proposes 2–3 additions. |
| `/ingest-book` | Breaks a book into citable entries for the library advisor (multi-session). |
| `/ingest-resource` | Turns an article, video, PDF or note into a linked vault note. |
| `/capture-insight` | Turns a story or lesson you just told into one permanent note. |
| `/pp-zotero-research-library` | Searches and syncs Zotero ("what did I add this week"). |
| `/ArXiv` | Searches arXiv papers by topic or ID, with AI overviews. |
| `/Science` | Scientific-method problem solving: hypotheses, falsifiable tests, iterate. |

### Data and sport
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/pp-catapult-openfield-connect` | Catapult GPS: ACWR, player load, weekly load reports. |
| `/pp-espn` | Scores, schedules, standings, game summaries. |
| `/game-film-timestamps` | Fixes Hudl/DVSport film-clip timestamps against ESPN play data. |
| **`/forecast-capture`** | Freezes the CFB Victory Model's Big 12 forecasts (Wednesday, Mac only, in season). |

### Meetings
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/meeting-prep <project>`** | One-screen brief before a meeting: what changed, what's open, did promises land. |
| **`/fireflies-intake`** | After meetings: renames, syncs and tags new transcripts into the vault, reports what came in. |
| `/meeting-sync` | The sync step alone (fireflies-intake and weekly-review call it). |
| `/name-meetings` | Proposes real titles for "Zoom Meeting"-style Fireflies titles. |
| `/pp-fireflies` | Searches transcripts across meetings ("who said…", stale action items). |

### Making things
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/research-in-5`** | One paper → 5-slide deck (dark + light), Teams post, staff email. Export on Windows. |
| `/five-slides-generator` | A Baylor-branded 5-slide deck on any topic. |
| `/html-to-pdf` | Prints a local HTML report to PDF (headless Chrome). |
| `/pbir-report-builder` | Builds Power BI report pages (PBIR JSON). |
| `/impeccable` | Frontend design: build, critique or polish a UI. |
| `/articulation-skill` | Explains a technical idea plainly for non-technical staff. |
| `/humanizer` | Removes the tells of AI-written text. |
| `/graphify <path>` | Knowledge graph of a folder or codebase, then answers questions from it. |

### Memory and "where did that go?"
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/memory-write` | "remember this", "forget that", "did we already…?" |
| `/landed [today\|week]` | Every file created or changed, by project, both machines. |
| `/where` | Files Claude wrote this session, with copy-path buttons. |
| `/session-handoff` | Chat-only summary before you `/clear` mid-session (closeout writes the durable one). |
| `/session-miner` | Finds lessons in recent sessions that never got saved. |
| `/improve-system` | Finds rot in the vault: stale, duplicate, contradicting notes. |
| `/brain-audit` | Scores the second brain out of 100 and proposes two builds (monthly, Mac). |

### End of day
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/interview-me`** | 10–15 min debrief: supervisor log, project-block question, reflections. |
| **`/harvest <project>`** | When something ships: output-ledger row + lesson notes. |
| **`/closeout`** | Fixes cards, commits and pushes everything, writes the handoff, gives the verdict. |

### Weekly and biweekly
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/weekly-review`** | Friday: syncs meetings, reviews the week, writes the note, runs the paused-project sweep. |
| **`/status-report`** | Every other Monday: email, one-page PDF and record for Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf. |

### Health and maintenance
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/claude-stack-doctor` | Read-only health check: scheduled jobs, memory pipeline, backups, machine handoff. |
| `/doctor-plus` | `claude doctor` plus a context-engineering audit of the workspace. |
| `/backup` | Runs the Mac's daily backup now (after the Mac was off at 21:00). |
| `/twins` | Hook or skill copies that differ between `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`/`~/.agents`. |
| `/encoding` | Finds and repairs BOM or garbled characters in config files. |
| `aios-audit` | (open Claude in `DEV/KeystoneOS`) Monthly audit of skills, hooks and memory. |
| `os-audit` | (in `DEV/KeystoneOS`) Read-only audit of routing, indexes and freshness. |

## Gaps found while writing this

## Every slash command, by where it fits

All 47 of your own skills, the two KeystoneOS project skills and the mod commands, as of
2026-10-03. Plugin skills (superpowers, mattpocock, codex, etc.) are not listed — type `/`
in Claude Code to see those. **Bold** = part of the daily or weekly ritual. Commands marked
*auto* fire on their own when the topic comes up; you rarely type them.

### Start of day
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/startup`** | Sit-down entry point: runs dev-sync, then reports where you left off and stops. |
| `/dev-sync` | The engine behind /startup: pulls config, skills and memory; mirrors memory across machines; syncs every repo; opens the board. Also "is everything pushed?" |
| `/pm` | Opens the live project board (starts it if needed). Same as `pm` in a shell. |
| `/slate` | Lists what the slate check flags (cap, charters, due steps). |
| `/repos` | Repos that are dirty, unpushed or behind origin. |
| `/jobs` | Scheduled jobs, the errors log, memory-search health. |
| `/next-steps off\|on` | Turns the three suggested-next-prompt buttons off or on. |

### Projects
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/project` | The registry: `idea`, `update`, `start`/`park`/`done`, `stage`, `rank`, `promote`; bare `/project` opens the board. |
| `/new-project` | Scaffolds a new repo (AGENTS, CLAUDE, STATUS), its private GitHub repo and Drive folder. |
| `/decision-audit` | Sorts the decisions you've been avoiding, names why they're stuck, then decides them with you. |
| `/ISA` | Writes an "Ideal State Artifact": what *done* means for a project, as testable criteria. |
| `/grill-with-ui` | A design interview in a browser page, each question with a recommendation. |
| `/project-triage` | Older daily HTML dashboard of every DEV folder. Overlaps the board; use `/pm`. |

### Research and knowledge
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/sports-science-research-grounding` | *auto* — answers sport-science, RTP, S&C and workload questions from Zotero first, labels outside sources. |
| `/library-advisor <domain> <q>` | Answers only from your ingested books, with citations. |
| `/library-review <domain>` | Finds gaps in a book domain and proposes 2–3 additions. |
| `/ingest-book` | Breaks a book into citable entries for the library advisor (multi-session). |
| `/ingest-resource` | Turns an article, video, PDF or note into a linked vault note. |
| `/capture-insight` | Turns a story or lesson you just told into one permanent note. |
| `/pp-zotero-research-library` | Searches and syncs Zotero ("what did I add this week"). |
| `/ArXiv` | Searches arXiv papers by topic or ID, with AI overviews. |
| `/Science` | Scientific-method problem solving: hypotheses, falsifiable tests, iterate. |

### Data and sport
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/pp-catapult-openfield-connect` | Catapult GPS: ACWR, player load, weekly load reports. |
| `/pp-espn` | Scores, schedules, standings, game summaries. |
| `/game-film-timestamps` | Fixes Hudl/DVSport film-clip timestamps against ESPN play data. |
| **`/forecast-capture`** | Freezes the CFB Victory Model's Big 12 forecasts (Wednesday, Mac only, in season). |

### Meetings
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/meeting-prep <project>`** | One-screen brief before a meeting: what changed, what's open, did promises land. |
| **`/fireflies-intake`** | After meetings: renames, syncs and tags new transcripts into the vault, reports what came in. |
| `/meeting-sync` | The sync step alone (fireflies-intake and weekly-review call it). |
| `/name-meetings` | Proposes real titles for "Zoom Meeting"-style Fireflies titles. |
| `/pp-fireflies` | Searches transcripts across meetings ("who said…", stale action items). |

### Making things
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/research-in-5`** | One paper → 5-slide deck (dark + light), Teams post, staff email. Export on Windows. |
| `/five-slides-generator` | A Baylor-branded 5-slide deck on any topic. |
| `/html-to-pdf` | Prints a local HTML report to PDF (headless Chrome). |
| `/pbir-report-builder` | Builds Power BI report pages (PBIR JSON). |
| `/impeccable` | Frontend design: build, critique or polish a UI. |
| `/articulation-skill` | Explains a technical idea plainly for non-technical staff. |
| `/humanizer` | Removes the tells of AI-written text. |
| `/graphify <path>` | Knowledge graph of a folder or codebase, then answers questions from it. |

### Memory and "where did that go?"
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/memory-write` | "remember this", "forget that", "did we already…?" |
| `/landed [today\|week]` | Every file created or changed, by project, both machines. |
| `/where` | Files Claude wrote this session, with copy-path buttons. |
| `/session-handoff` | Chat-only summary before you `/clear` mid-session (closeout writes the durable one). |
| `/session-miner` | Finds lessons in recent sessions that never got saved. |
| `/improve-system` | Finds rot in the vault: stale, duplicate, contradicting notes. |
| `/brain-audit` | Scores the second brain out of 100 and proposes two builds (monthly, Mac). |

### End of day
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/interview-me`** | 10–15 min debrief: supervisor log, project-block question, reflections. |
| **`/harvest <project>`** | When something ships: output-ledger row + lesson notes. |
| **`/closeout`** | Fixes cards, commits and pushes everything, writes the handoff, gives the verdict. |

### Weekly and biweekly
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **`/weekly-review`** | Friday: syncs meetings, reviews the week, writes the note, runs the paused-project sweep. |
| **`/status-report`** | Every other Monday: email, one-page PDF and record for Kenny Boyd and Chris Ruf. |

### Health and maintenance
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/claude-stack-doctor` | Read-only health check: scheduled jobs, memory pipeline, backups, machine handoff. |
| `/doctor-plus` | `claude doctor` plus a context-engineering audit of the workspace. |
| `/backup` | Runs the Mac's daily backup now (after the Mac was off at 21:00). |
| `/twins` | Hook or skill copies that differ between `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`/`~/.agents`. |
| `/encoding` | Finds and repairs BOM or garbled characters in config files. |
| `aios-audit` | (open Claude in `DEV/KeystoneOS`) Monthly audit of skills, hooks and memory. |
| `os-audit` | (in `DEV/KeystoneOS`) Read-only audit of routing, indexes and freshness. |
